topics.framing_note: KEYSTONE — Douglass is named explicitly in moral_vision §1, §3.6 and §8 as a bank exemplar (the Rochester July 5 1852 'What to the Slave is the Fourth of July?' speech). Cool-fact-is-answer: his exact argument — NOT that the Declaration was wrong, but that America was betraying its own true founding principles (the sophisticated natural-rights move, quoted in moral_vision §8 as the bar). The escaped slave who taught himself to read and became America's conscience. Virtue at cost. HIGHEST weight.

topics.name: Harriet Tubman and the Underground Railroad
topics.scope: Conductor, repeated rescue missions, Moses
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2, named in framework §2. Virtue-by-example (courage at cost, moral_vision §2). Cool-fact-is-answer: 'I never lost a passenger' — the conductor who returned to slave territory roughly 13 times to free ~70 people, carried a pistol, later scouted for the Union army at the Combahee Raid. Show the courage, don't preach it. American story.

topics.name: Reconstruction and the Reconstruction Amendments
topics.scope: 13th/14th/15th Amendments, KKK, Jim Crow's rise
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2 — 'the unfinished struggle over what freedom would mean'. Cool-fact-is-answer: the three amendments and what each did (13th abolished slavery, 14th equal protection/citizenship, 15th the vote regardless of race), then the honest tragedy: the KKK's terror and Jim Crow's rise as the promise was rolled back. State the failure plainly per moral_vision §3.6 (American failures stated as fact, not theatricalized) — and frame it as betrayal of the founding principles, the Douglass/Lincoln natural-rights line, NOT a 1619-style indictment of the founding itself (framework forbidden #3).

topics.name: The transcontinental railroad and the golden spike
topics.scope: 1869 Promontory Summit, Chinese and Irish labor
topics.framing_note: Pillar 1 American achievement — the iron rail binding a continent. Cool-fact-is-answer: the golden spike at Promontory Summit, Utah, May 10 1869, the two railroads meeting. Honor the Chinese (Central Pacific) and Irish (Union Pacific) labor that built it as the achievement-by-real-people it was (moral_vision ordinary-ingenuity), stating the dangerous conditions plainly without anti-Western framing.

topics.name: Westward expansion and the Plains Indian Wars
topics.scope: Little Bighorn 1876, Custer, Sitting Bull, Crazy Horse
topics.framing_note: Honest record per moral_vision §3.6 (Trail of Tears, Wounded Knee named among American failures) + framework §5 'human cost' stated plainly. Cool-fact-is-answer: Sitting Bull's vision and Crazy Horse's tactics annihilating Custer's command at Little Bighorn 1876, then the tragic close at Wounded Knee 1890. Present the Plains nations on their own terms (skilled, formidable), the conquest's human cost as fact — NOT 'savages' framing, NOT theatricalized self-loathing. Honest comparison, both the military drama and the displacement.

topics.name: The Gilded Age industrialists
topics.scope: Carnegie steel, Rockefeller oil, Vanderbilt rails
topics.framing_note: Present on its own terms with the genuine dual record (moral_vision §1.7) — Carnegie's steel empire and the Bessemer-driven productivity that built modern America AND the ruthless tactics + Homestead strike; Rockefeller's Standard Oil efficiency AND the monopoly. Cool-fact-is-answer: the named achievement (Carnegie rising from bobbin boy, the Gospel of Wealth and his libraries; Rockefeller's refining efficiency that cut kerosene prices). Steel-man both the creative and the predatory; avoid the lazy 'robber baron' caricature AND avoid hagiography.

topics.name: The Scramble for Africa and the Berlin Conference
topics.scope: 1884-85 partition, European powers carve a continent
topics.source: AP World Unit 6 state expansion; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Honest record stated plainly (moral_vision §4 'state what happened, don't editorialize'). Cool-fact-is-answer: Europe carving up a continent with rulers on a map at the Berlin Conference 1884-85, no African present; the named atrocity floor — Leopold II's Congo Free State (rubber terror, severed hands, millions dead) as a documented horror. State the colonial violence as fact per §3.4 'part of the same honest record'. No anti-Western inherent-condemnation framing (§9) — name the specific perpetrators and the specific Western critics who exposed it (E.D. Morel, Roger Casement).

topics.name: The British Raj in India
topics.scope: 1857 rebellion, Crown rule 1858, jewel in the crown
topics.source: HISTORY_TEMPLATES Pillar 5 India; AP World Unit 6
topics.framing_note: Honest dual record (moral_vision §1.7, §3.4) — the 1857 Rebellion (Sepoy Mutiny, the greased-cartridge spark), Crown rule 1858, the 'jewel in the crown'. State both: the railways/rule-of-law/English-language institutions AND the famines, the extraction. Pairs with framework §5 — Bentinck banning suttee 1829 under Carey's pressure, Sleeman suppressing Thuggee: honest pre-modern brutality ended by named reformers (decomposed into its own injected cell). Present India's civilization on its own terms, not as foil.

topics.name: The Opium Wars and China's century of humiliation
topics.scope: 1839-42 + 1856-60, treaty ports, Hong Kong ceded
topics.source: HISTORY_TEMPLATES Pillar 5 China; AP World Unit 6
topics.framing_note: Honest record stated plainly — Britain forcing a drug trade on China by gunboat (moral_vision §4). Cool-fact-is-answer: Commissioner Lin Zexu dumping 1,000+ tons of opium into the sea at Canton 1839, the British response, Hong Kong ceded, the treaty ports. State the British wrong as fact, no euphemism — this is honest about Western failure per §3.4. Present China's grievance on its own terms (the 'century of humiliation'). Sets up the Taiping and the later Chinese story.

topics.name: Taiping Rebellion
topics.scope: 1850-64, 20M+ dead, Christian-messianic uprising
topics.framing_note: The deadliest war of the entire 19th century (20M+ dead) — framework Pillar 5 names it. Cool-fact-is-answer: Hong Xiuquan, the failed examination candidate who believed he was Jesus's younger brother and launched a civil war that killed more than the entire American Civil War many times over. Present on its own terms, the staggering toll stated as fact. A scale-of-suffering most kids never hear of.

topics.name: Commodore Perry's black ships open Japan
topics.scope: 1853 fleet ends sakoku isolation
topics.framing_note: Pillar 5 — American warships ending 250 years of Japanese seclusion. Cool-fact-is-answer: Perry's black ships steaming into Edo Bay 1853, the gunboat diplomacy that cracked sakoku open. Present on its own terms; the hinge that triggers the Meiji Restoration. Story-led, named moment.

topics.name: The Meiji Restoration and Japan's modernization
topics.scope: 1868 restoration, rapid industrialization, end of samurai
topics.source: HISTORY_TEMPLATES Pillar 5 Japan; AP World Unit 6
topics.framing_note: Pillar 5 — a nation that industrialized in a single generation, on its own terms (moral_vision §4, non-Western civilizations as real achievements not foils). Cool-fact-is-answer: the 1868 restoration of the emperor, the deliberate wholesale adoption of Western industry/law/military, and the end of the samurai (the Satsuma Rebellion, the last stand). A genuinely astonishing self-transformation. Substantive, admiring, on Japan's own terms.

topics.name: Social Darwinism and the civilizing-mission rationale
topics.scope: 'Survival of fittest' applied to nations, white man's burden
topics.source: AP World Unit 6.1 rationales for imperialism
topics.framing_note: Present the IDEOLOGY for recognition, attributed to its proponents, NOT adopted (moral_vision §6 advocacy-framing rule fires hard here). Frame as: the rationalizations Europeans USED to justify ruling others — Spencer's 'survival of the fittest' misapplied to nations, Kipling's 'white man's burden'. The bank teaches the kid to RECOGNIZE this as the pseudo-scientific self-justification it was (§3.7 — biological variance never extrapolated to group moral worth; this is the historical example of exactly that error). Honest history of a bad idea, named and dated, never endorsed and never used to indict the West as inherently evil (§9) — it indicts a specific false ideology.

topics.name: Adwa: Ethiopia defeats Italy
topics.scope: 1896 victory, only African state to repel conquest
topics.framing_note: Pillar 5 — an African army crushing a European invasion, on its own terms (moral_vision §4). Cool-fact-is-answer: Menelik II and Empress Taytu's forces routing the Italians at Adwa 1896, keeping Ethiopia the one African state never colonized in the Scramble. A genuine military triumph told straight, the named victory as the answer. Present Ethiopia's achievement admiringly.

topics.name: The Suez Canal
topics.scope: 1869 opening, link of Mediterranean and Red Sea
topics.framing_note: Pillar 1/6 engineering wonder + geopolitics. Cool-fact-is-answer: de Lesseps's canal opening 1869 joining the Mediterranean and Red Sea, cutting the voyage to India by thousands of miles, and Britain's later purchase of the shares that made it imperial lifeline. Mechanism + consequence. Present on its own terms.

topics.name: Rorke's Drift and the Anglo-Zulu War
topics.scope: 1879 Isandlwana defeat then 11 Victoria Crosses
topics.framing_note: Pillar 3 iconic moment, BOTH sides honored. Cool-fact-is-answer: the Zulu impi annihilating a British column at Isandlwana 1879 (a spear-armed kingdom shocking the Empire), then ~150 men holding the mission station at Rorke's Drift, earning 11 Victoria Crosses. Present the Zulu as the formidable, disciplined army they were (not foil) AND the defenders' stand. Story-led drama, named victories on both sides.

topics.name: Darwin and On the Origin of Species
topics.scope: 1859 evolution by natural selection, Galapagos finches
topics.framing_note: Pillar 1/6 — the book that transformed how we see life. Cool-fact-is-answer: natural selection, the Galapagos finches, the Beagle voyage, and the drama (Darwin sitting on the theory 20 years, then Wallace's letter forcing the joint 1858 announcement). Discovery-recognition (how-we-know). Present the science straight, mechanism-wonder. NOTE moral_vision treats science and faith as non-opponents (§3.4) — present Darwin as discovery, not as a weapon against religion; keep contemporary creation/evolution policy debates OUT (dated-topical rule).

topics.name: Pasteur, germ theory, and vaccines
topics.scope: Germ theory, anthrax 1881, rabies vaccine 1885
topics.framing_note: Pillar 6 discovery + mechanism wonder (the immune mechanism is REAL proven biology — honored per the science-stance memory). Cool-fact-is-answer: Pasteur proving germs cause disease (the swan-neck flask defeating spontaneous generation), the anthrax field trial 1881, the rabies vaccine saving young Joseph Meister 1885. Discovery-recognition, virtue (the public risk of the field trial). Keep it to the 19th-c scientific achievement — do NOT import contemporary vaccine-policy contestation (that's science-bank, present-day, out of this historical strand).

topics.name: The Eiffel Tower and the 1889 World's Fair
topics.scope: Built for exposition, slated for demolition
topics.framing_note: Pillar 1 art/architecture + surprise-reversal. Cool-fact-is-answer: the iron icon built for the 1889 Exposition, denounced by Paris artists, slated for demolition after 20 years — saved because it made a perfect radio antenna. Wonder of engineering + the reversal that it was almost torn down. Light, celebratory; Western achievement.

topics.name: Seneca Falls and the women's rights movement
topics.scope: 1848 convention, Declaration of Sentiments, suffrage
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2 — the organized fight for women's rights born from the natural-rights tradition. Cool-fact-is-answer: the 1848 Seneca Falls Convention and the Declaration of Sentiments deliberately echoing the Declaration of Independence ('all men and women are created equal'), Stanton and Mott, Douglass the lone prominent man backing the suffrage resolution. Frame as the founding principles being extended/claimed — the same Douglass natural-rights move, NOT a grievance-against-the-founding frame. Present on its own terms.

topics.name: The Industrial Revolution as the Great Enrichment — the hockey-stick escape from poverty
topics.scope: ~1800 inflection: living standards, life expectancy, and real wages begin their unprecedented sustained rise after millennia of flat subsistence; market capital accumulation as the engine
topics.framing_note: The consensus list itemizes the inventions but MISSES the headline the vision demands: industrialization was the most important good-news event in human history — the moment ordinary people began escaping the grinding poverty universal for all prior history. Cool-fact-is-answer: the named inflection (the 'hockey stick' of GDP/life-expectancy bending sharply up around 1800), the surprise-reversal that the 'dark satanic mills' era was when child mortality and starvation began their long collapse. Market-driven capital accumulation as the engine (moral_vision §3.3). Wonder-first, honestly stated — the human cost (child labor) is covered in its own cells; this cell carries the progress the standard curriculum buries under the misery narrative. Attribute interpretive claims; let the data carry it, no triumphalism.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §2 commands celebrating 'the real human progress' and the framework's Pillar 1 is HEAVIEST; the consensus list has the gadgets but no cell stating that the Industrial Revolution lifted humanity out of universal poverty — the single most important fact about the era and a core dual-commitment the vision exists to transmit.

topics.name: Bastiat and the seen-versus-unseen — the broken-window fallacy (1850)
topics.scope: Frederic Bastiat, 'That Which Is Seen and That Which Is Not Seen' 1850, the broken-window parable, the satirical candlemakers' petition
topics.framing_note: Present the reasoning move for recognition, attributed to Bastiat ('Bastiat argued...'). Cool-fact-is-answer: the broken-window parable (breaking a window does NOT enrich the town — it merely hides the bread or book the shopkeeper would otherwise have bought) and the satirical Candlemakers' Petition demanding protection from the unfair competition of the sun. The 19th-century French economist who is the bank's named exemplar of seen/unseen reasoning. Teach-before-test honored (introduce Bastiat as the figure). Wonder-driven, not polemical.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.3 names 'Bastiat's seen/unseen' as required coverage and §1 places Bastiat in the bank's intellectual lineage; he is a mid-19th-century figure squarely in this strand yet entirely absent from the consensus list, which over-weights Marx as the era's economic voice without the classical-liberal counterweight the vision mandates.

topics.name: The internal African slave trade and the Royal Navy West Africa Squadron
topics.scope: Africans enslaving Africans for coastal kingdoms (Asante, Dahomey) and the Arab-Swahili trade (Tippu Tip's Zanzibar network into the 1890s); the Royal Navy squadron 1808-1860s freeing ~150,000 at sea; Livingstone's documentation
topics.framing_note: Honest record stated plainly per framework §5, NO 'savages' framing, NO sensationalism. State the fact the standard curriculum omits: the slave trade had a large internal-African and Arab-Swahili supply side that long predated and outlasted the Atlantic trade (Tippu Tip operating into the 1890s), and it was the Royal Navy West Africa Squadron — at real cost in sailors' lives to malaria — that hunted slavers across the Atlantic 1808-1860s, freeing roughly 150,000 people. Pair with Livingstone exposing the East African trade. The Wilberforce cell legislates abolition; THIS cell is the enforcement and the honest supply-side record (§3.4 imago-Dei crusade in action).
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §5 explicitly REQUIRES the internal African slave trade + Royal Navy West Africa Squadron as honest pre-modern brutality paired with the Western intervention that ended it; the consensus list covers legislative abolition (Wilberforce) but omits both the honest supply-side record and the naval enforcement the framework names by name.

topics.name: Suttee, Thuggee, and foot-binding ended by named reformers
topics.scope: Hindu widow-burning banned by Lord William Bentinck 1829 under William Carey's pressure; the Thuggee strangulation cult suppressed by William Sleeman in the 1830s-40s; Chinese foot-binding ended by missionary-reformer collaboration
topics.framing_note: Honest record, stated as fact, NO condescension and NO 'exotic East' framing (moral_vision §4) — paired with the named reformers who ended each practice. Cool-fact-is-answer: Bentinck's 1829 ban on suttee, Sleeman's detective campaign that broke the Thuggee cult (possibly 2M murders over centuries), the missionary-Chinese-reformer alliance against foot-binding. These are 19th-century reforms (Bentinck 1829, Sleeman 1830s-40s) squarely in this strand. Honest comparison, not condescension (§4): some traditions developed the reform impulse, and the bank says so by naming who acted — without inherent-condemnation of any culture (§9).
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §5 names suttee/Bentinck, Thuggee/Sleeman, and foot-binding specifically as required honest-brutality-plus-Western-intervention content, and these are 19th-century events; the consensus list (which has the Raj only as a container) omits these named reform moments the framework mandates.

topics.name: Cyrus Field and the Atlantic telegraph cable
topics.scope: The 1858 and successful 1866 transatlantic cables; instant Europe-America communication; repeated failures before triumph; the Great Eastern laying it
topics.framing_note: Pillar 1/6 wonder + virtue-by-example (perseverance through repeated failure). Cool-fact-is-answer: Cyrus Field's transatlantic cable — the 1858 line that worked for weeks then died, and the 1866 success that finally let a message cross the ocean in minutes instead of the ten days a ship took. Lead with the wonder of the Atlantic annihilated and the drama of the failed attempts. A staking-everything-on-a-calculation story the vision prizes (cf. the Wright brothers).
topics.rationale: The consensus list's telegraph cell is domestic (Morse 1844) and stops at the land line; the transatlantic cable — the moment two continents were joined in real time — is a Pillar 1/6 wonder and a virtue-by-perseverance story the vision celebrates, materially under-covered by the existing entries.

topics.name: Faraday, Maxwell, and the conquest of electromagnetism
topics.scope: Faraday's induction (1831) and field concept; Maxwell's equations (1865) unifying electricity, magnetism, and light; both devout Christians
topics.framing_note: Pillar 6 mechanism-wonder + Western-tradition-as-achievement. Cool-fact-is-answer: Faraday — the self-taught bookbinder's apprentice who discovered electromagnetic induction (move a magnet near a wire, get a current: the principle behind every generator) — and Maxwell predicting from pure equations that light itself IS an electromagnetic wave, unifying three phenomena. Both were serious Christians (moral_vision §3.4 names them); present the science straight, the faith as biographical fact, never as opponents. The theoretical foundation that made the entire electrical age (Edison, Tesla) possible. Beauty-of-mechanism, why it works.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.4 names Faraday and Maxwell explicitly as believer-scientists; the consensus list has the APPLIED electrical boom (Bell/Edison, war of currents) but omits the foundational 19th-century physics — a Pillar 1+6 gap the vision flags by naming these two men.

topics.name: Mendel and the birth of genetics
topics.scope: Gregor Mendel's pea-plant experiments (1856-1863) establishing the laws of inheritance; work ignored until rediscovered ~1900
topics.framing_note: Pillar 6 discovery + surprise-reversal + Western-tradition-as-achievement. Cool-fact-is-answer: the Augustinian friar Gregor Mendel counting tens of thousands of pea plants in a monastery garden to discover the hidden math of heredity (dominant and recessive traits) — work so far ahead of its time it was ignored for 35 years until three botanists independently rediscovered it in 1900. A monk founding genetics (moral_vision §3.4 names Mendel; Christianity and science as non-opponents). Discovery + the reversal of the overlooked genius.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.4 names Mendel explicitly among the believer-scientists the bank honors; the foundational genetics discovery of the 19th century is absent from the consensus list, which covers Darwin and Pasteur but skips Mendel — a Pillar 6 + believer-scientist gap the vision mandates.

strands.strand: World War I & the interwar years

topics.name: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
topics.scope: Sarajevo 1914 spark of WWI
topics.framing_note: Story-led per voice rules: the wrong turn down Franz Josef Street, Princip stepping off the curb, the chain of contingency. The cool fact is the answer (the sandwich-shop wrong turn, the failed grenade earlier that morning) per HISTORY_FRAMEWORK 'cool fact is the answer.' No 'this shows how fragile peace was' weasel closer (moral_vision anti-pattern; SHARED §15). Present the human accident, not a thesis about determinism.

topics.name: The July Crisis and alliance system
topics.scope: Alliances drag Europe into war
topics.source: AP Euro, AP World, Core Knowledge
topics.framing_note: Mechanism over slogan: how mobilization timetables and the blank-check ultimatum turned a Balkan murder into a continental war. Steelman the decisions of real statesmen under real pressure (framework core principle) rather than 'everyone blundered.' Avoid the abstract 'entangling alliances' lecture; anchor to a named moment (Austrian ultimatum to Serbia, German blank cheque). No verdict-imposing stem on war-guilt — present the cascade.

topics.name: Trench warfare and the Western Front
topics.scope: No man's land, stalemate, mud
topics.source: Core Knowledge, AP World, cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Concrete-over-abstract (voice rules): the duckboards, the rats, the 'over the top' whistle, the parapet. This is honest pre-modern-into-modern brutality stated plainly, not theatricalized (moral_vision §4). The cool specific is the answer (trench foot, the firestep, 'Tommy'). Show the human endurance without preaching 'war is hell.'

topics.name: New weapons of WWI
topics.scope: Machine guns, gas, tanks, planes
topics.framing_note: The beauty/horror of mechanism (moral_vision §2 'beauty of mechanism'): WHY the machine gun made the offensive suicidal, WHY chlorine then mustard gas changed the air itself, the Mark I tank crossing trenches. Industrial killing stated as fact. Specific named first-uses are the answer (chlorine at Ypres 1915, tanks at the Somme 1916). Honest, not cynical.

topics.name: Battle of the Somme
topics.scope: 1916, worst single-day British losses
topics.framing_note: Pillar 3 great-battles, story-led with stakes + consequence (framework). The singular number belongs in the STEM as the hook, not the answer (SHARED §19; moral_vision §2) — ~57,470 British casualties on July 1 leads, and the knowable specific (the Pals battalions, the creeping barrage, the whistle at 7:30am) is the answer. Honest slaughter, not 'futility' editorializing.

topics.name: Battle of Verdun
topics.scope: 1916, 'They shall not pass'
topics.framing_note: Courage and endurance shown by example (moral_vision §2, framework 'drama'). 'Ils ne passeront pas' and the Voie Sacrée supply road as named things (the answer), not 'symbol of French resolve' abstraction. Falkenhayn's explicit attrition aim ('bleed France white') is the grim mechanism. Pétain's rotation system. State the meatgrinder honestly.

topics.name: Gallipoli campaign
topics.scope: 1915 failed Dardanelles landing
topics.framing_note: Honest about a Western/Allied failure stated plainly (moral_vision §9 not-triumphalist): Churchill's plan, the botched landings, the cliffs. The ANZAC legend and Mustafa Kemal's 'I order you to die' are the named cool facts (answers). Birth of both the ANZAC identity and Turkish nationalism. Don't sanitize the disaster; don't theatricalize it.

topics.name: Sinking of the Lusitania
topics.scope: 1915 U-boat attack, civilian deaths
topics.framing_note: Part of the American-entry arc (Pillar 2). State the facts plainly: 1,198 dead including 128 Americans, the contested munitions cargo, unrestricted submarine warfare. The named specific (18 minutes to sink, the second internal explosion) is the answer. Honest, not propagandistic — note Germany had warned passengers, without adopting either government's spin.

topics.name: America enters World War I
topics.scope: Zimmermann Telegram, doughboys, 1917
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2 (HEAVY) — the American story. The decoded Zimmermann Telegram (Mexico offered Texas/Arizona/New Mexico) and the AEF tipping the balance are the named cool facts. Celebrate the decisive American contribution honestly (moral_vision §3.6) — Belleau Wood, the doughboys, Pershing — without triumphalism. Room 40 codebreaking as ordinary ingenuity.

topics.name: The Christmas Truce of 1914
topics.scope: Soldiers stop fighting, share carols
topics.framing_note: Virtue and shared humanity shown by example, not preached (moral_vision §5, §2 courage/decency). The named specifics — 'Stille Nacht' drifting across no man's land, the football in no man's land, exchanged buttons and cigarettes — are the answer. Warm but precise; resist the temptation to moralize 'if only they'd kept refusing.' Let the human moment stand.

topics.name: The Red Baron and aerial dogfights
topics.scope: Manfred von Richthofen, flying aces
topics.framing_note: Wonder + ordinary ingenuity (moral_vision §2): the first air war, the Fokker Dr.I triplane, 80 victories, the all-red plane, the Flying Circus. Named things are the answer. A thrilling T1 hook done straight — the chivalry-of-the-air alongside the lethality. No condescension to the era; these were brave men in canvas planes.

topics.name: Armenian Genocide
topics.scope: 1915 Ottoman mass killing
topics.framing_note: Show the evil plainly (framework forbids sanitizing genocide; moral_vision §4 honest-not-cynical). ~1.5M killed; the death marches into the Syrian desert; April 24 1915 arrest of Constantinople intellectuals. Raphael Lemkin later coined 'genocide' partly studying this (named cool fact / answer). State it as established fact — the bank does not soft-pedal mass killing. Henry Morgenthau Sr.'s eyewitness dispatches.

topics.name: Lawrence of Arabia and the Arab Revolt
topics.scope: Desert war against the Ottomans
topics.framing_note: Drama of a vivid individual (framework Pillar 6). The Aqaba attack from the desert side, the railway raids, the camel charge are the named actions (answers). Honest about the betrayal: the Sykes-Picot secret carve-up that contradicted promises to the Arabs (moral_vision §4 honest-not-preachy) — stated as fact, seeding the modern Middle East. Romantic figure presented with the complication intact.

topics.name: Armistice of November 11, 1918
topics.scope: Eleventh hour, war ends
topics.framing_note: The named specific is the answer: 11am on 11/11, the railway carriage in Compiègne forest (the same carriage Hitler would later demand for France's 1940 surrender — a foreshadowing cool fact). Origin of Remembrance/Veterans Day. Note the tragedy of men dying in the final hours. Concrete, warm, factual.

topics.name: The human cost and shell shock
topics.scope: Casualties, a lost generation, trauma
topics.framing_note: Honest record stated plainly (moral_vision §4). ~9-10M military dead; the 'lost generation'; shell shock named and recognized for the first time. Show the human wound by example (the trembling, the mute soldiers) rather than a 'trauma awareness' lecture. The named specific is the answer. Avoid anachronistic clinical framing — present how the era itself grasped it.

topics.name: Treaty of Versailles
topics.scope: 1919 peace, war-guilt, reparations
topics.framing_note: The Big Four at Paris, Article 231 war-guilt clause, the 132-billion-gold-mark reparations, the Hall of Mirrors signing. Present the serious debate honestly: the harsh-peace-seeded-WWII thesis AND the revisionist case, without imposing a verdict (moral_vision no-verdict-on-contested). Keynes's 'Economic Consequences of the Peace' is the named critique (answer-worthy). Foch's 'this is not peace but an armistice for twenty years' — eerily exact, a cool fact.

topics.name: Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points
topics.scope: Self-determination, idealist peace plan
topics.source: AP US, AP World, Core Knowledge
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2 American story. Present Wilson's idealism on its own terms (self-determination, open covenants) AND why it foundered against European realpolitik and the Senate — honest, not hagiographic (framework forbids sanitizing). Clemenceau's quip 'God Himself was content with ten commandments; Wilson gives us fourteen' is the named cool fact. The self-determination principle's unintended consequences stated as fact.

topics.name: The League of Nations
topics.scope: First world body, no US, toothless
topics.framing_note: State the structural facts: the US Senate's rejection (Lodge, the irreconcilables), the unanimity rule, no army — and the failures to come (Manchuria, Abyssinia). Anti-totalitarian lens available (moral_vision §1.2): collective security that cannot enforce is theater. Honest about the noble intention and the fatal design. The named specific (which great power never joined despite its president founding it) is the answer.

topics.name: Redrawing the map of Europe
topics.scope: New nations, fallen empires post-1918
topics.framing_note: Four empires fall (Romanov, Hohenzollern, Habsburg, Ottoman) — a hinge of Western history (Pillar 1). The named new nations (Poland reborn after 123 years, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia) are the cool facts/answers. State honestly that drawing borders over mixed populations planted future conflicts (moral_vision §4 honest-not-cynical) — Sudeten Germans, the Polish Corridor — without editorializing.

topics.name: Russian Revolution of 1917
topics.scope: Tsar falls, Bolsheviks seize power
topics.framing_note: PILLAR 4, HEAVY BY DESIGN. CRITICAL: do NOT romanticize the Bolshevik seizure. Distinguish the February liberal revolution from the October Bolshevik COUP (a minority faction seizing power, dissolving the freely elected Constituent Assembly in January 1918 by force). Lenin's sealed train from Switzerland (German-funded), 'All power to the soviets,' the Winter Palace are named facts/answers. Marxism-as-implementation begins here — the regime that would produce 65-100M deaths (moral_vision §3.1). Steelman the revolutionaries' grievances (war, hunger, autocracy) without adopting their self-justification; no 'workers' paradise' framing. The promise vs. what was actually built.

topics.name: Fall of the Romanovs and Rasputin
topics.scope: Last Tsar, mad monk, execution
topics.framing_note: Drama done straight (Pillar 6). Rasputin's near-impossible-to-kill death (poison, shots, the icy Neva) and the Ipatiev House cellar execution of the whole family July 1918 are the named cool facts/answers. State the Bolshevik murder of children plainly (moral_vision §4 — show the evil) — the regime executed the Tsar's daughters and hemophiliac son. The Anastasia survival myth (later DNA-debunked) as the mystery hook. No condescension to 'superstitious' Russia.

topics.name: Rise of Stalin and the USSR
topics.scope: Five-Year Plans, purges, terror
topics.framing_note: PILLAR 4 CORE — the heaviest truth-telling cell in this strand. Count the terror honestly with specific tolls and named perpetrators (moral_vision §3.1; framework Pillar 4): the Great Purge / Yezhovshchina 1936-38, the show trials, NKVD execution quotas, the decapitation of the Red Army (Tukhachevsky). The Gulag as a SYSTEM, not an excess. NO false equivalence, NO 'both sides,' NO establishment soft-pedaling — distractors may include the soft-pedaled 'about half a million' so the kid picks the honest scale. Steelman nothing about the terror; the bodies were counted. Note the Hayek/Mises calculation-problem lens (moral_vision §3.2) — the Five-Year Plans' chaos was predicted.

topics.name: The Spanish Flu pandemic of 1918
topics.scope: Deadliest flu, killed millions worldwide
topics.framing_note: Wonder/horror of nature stated plainly. Killed ~50M+ (more than the war), the 'Spanish' misnomer (neutral Spain merely reported it freely while combatants censored), the unusual W-curve killing healthy young adults via cytokine storm. The named specific is the answer. Honest, not moralizing; this is the science-adjacent fact-as-hook handled as history. No present-day pandemic-policy drift (moral_vision dated-topical / SHARED §18).

topics.name: The Roaring Twenties
topics.scope: Jazz Age, flappers, boom
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2 — celebrate the genuine American dynamism honestly (moral_vision §3.6 American experiment). Jazz (Armstrong), the Charleston, flappers, radio, the Model T assembly line, electrification spreading. The Harlem Renaissance (Hughes, Ellington) as real cultural achievement included on its own terms. The named cool fact is the answer. Available counterweight: the decade's real economic growth under low taxes (the Coolidge boom) — present as fact, not advocacy.

topics.name: Prohibition and the gangster era
topics.scope: 18th Amendment, speakeasies, Al Capone
topics.source: Core Knowledge, AP US, cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: A clean seen-vs-unseen / unintended-consequences case (moral_vision economics lens, incentive recognition) presented as history: banning booze created the speakeasy, bootlegging empires, and Capone — then the St. Valentine's Day Massacre 1929 and the repeal. The named specific (Capone jailed not for murder but for tax evasion; Eliot Ness's Untouchables) is the cool-fact answer. State the policy-backfire as fact, not a libertarian sermon.

topics.name: Charles Lindbergh and the age of flight
topics.scope: 1927 first solo Atlantic flight
topics.framing_note: Courage staked on a calculation (moral_vision §2 — the Wright-brothers archetype; §4 'ordinary ingenuity'). The Spirit of St. Louis, 33.5 hours awake alone over the Atlantic, no front windshield (a periscope to see ahead) are the named cool facts/answers. Celebrate the era's greatest individual feat done straight. Keep it to the flight — Lindbergh's later political controversies are out of this strand's scope.

topics.name: Wall Street Crash of 1929
topics.scope: Black Tuesday, market collapse
topics.framing_note: The named days (Black Thursday Oct 24, Black Tuesday Oct 29), margin buying, the ticker running hours behind. CRITICAL vision lens (moral_vision §3.3 Austrian coverage AT LEAST EQUAL): make the Austrian Business Cycle account available — the 1920s Fed credit expansion fueling the bubble (Mises/Hayek predicted the bust) — presented as a serious position alongside other accounts, NOT as the only one and NOT as advocacy. Steelman each causal theory (moral_vision §6). The crash as trigger-not-sole-cause of the Depression.

topics.name: The Great Depression
topics.scope: Mass unemployment, breadlines, global slump
topics.framing_note: State the human facts plainly: 25% US unemployment, breadlines, Hoovervilles, global bank failures, the gold-standard transmission worldwide. Vision balance (moral_vision §3.3): the policy-response debate is GENUINELY contested — present the Keynesian, monetarist (Friedman-Schwartz: the Fed let the money supply collapse), and Austrian accounts each at their strongest, no verdict imposed (no-verdict-on-contested). Smoot-Hawley tariffs deepening the global slump is the named consequence/answer. The reshaping of world politics (it fed extremism) stated as fact.

topics.name: The Dust Bowl
topics.scope: 1930s drought, Okies, dust storms
topics.framing_note: Ecological + human disaster stated concretely (voice rules). Black Sunday April 14 1935, the rollers of dust burying farms, the Okie migration to California, dust reaching Washington DC. The named specific is the answer. The over-plowing of the prairie sod as the mechanism (a real ingenuity-gone-wrong story). Honest human suffering; no eco-moralizing overlay.

topics.name: FDR and the New Deal
topics.scope: Relief programs, fireside chats
topics.framing_note: Pillar 2. Present FDR's response and its scale honestly — the fireside chats, the bank holiday, the CCC/WPA/TVA, Social Security — AND the serious contested debate it opened (moral_vision §3.9, §3.3, §6: steelman both sides). The New Deal as the moment the federal government's role transformed: present the FDR/positive-rights case (the 1944 Second Bill of Rights) at full strength AND the Hayek/critics' case that guaranteed goods become claims on others — no verdict imposed. Court-packing fight as the named episode. Honest, not hagiographic; not a tract either direction.

topics.name: Rise of Mussolini and Italian Fascism
topics.scope: March on Rome, Blackshirts, Il Duce
topics.source: AP Euro, AP World, Core Knowledge
topics.framing_note: Anti-totalitarian foundation (moral_vision §1.2). The March on Rome 1922, the Blackshirts, 'Il Duce,' the corporate state, 'everything within the state, nothing outside the state.' Present fascism's actual ideology accurately and seriously (moral_vision §6 no strawmen) — its origins partly on the revolutionary left, its statism — so kids RECOGNIZE the structure, not a cartoon. The first fascist state and the model Hitler studied. The named specific is the answer.

topics.name: Hitler's rise to power
topics.scope: Weimar collapse, Nazis, 1933 chancellor
topics.framing_note: Anti-totalitarian core (moral_vision §1.2). How a constitutional democracy was dismantled legally-then-violently: the failed 1923 Beer Hall Putsch, Mein Kampf written in Landsberg prison, the 1932 electoral surge amid Depression, the Jan 1933 chancellorship, the Reichstag Fire, the Enabling Act. Show the MECHANISM by which democracy votes/slides into dictatorship — the recognition skill (moral_vision §2). Named specifics are answers. No strawman of why Germans followed; state the real conditions (Depression, Versailles resentment, Communist street-fear) honestly without excusing.

topics.name: Weimar Republic and hyperinflation
topics.scope: German democracy, worthless money, 1923
topics.framing_note: A vivid sound-money lesson as history (moral_vision §3.3 Austrian, fiat-dies recognition). Wheelbarrows of marks, banknotes burned for heat / used as wallpaper, 4.2 TRILLION marks to the dollar by Nov 1923, the Rentenmark stabilization. The named specific (the wheelbarrow, the price doubling within hours) is the cool-fact answer. Present the monetary mechanism (printing to pay reparations) as fact. The instability that fed extremism stated plainly — no sermon.

topics.name: Nazi ideology and the Nuremberg Laws
topics.scope: Antisemitism, propaganda, state terror
topics.framing_note: Show the racist machinery plainly (framework forbids sanitizing; moral_vision §3.7 racism unacceptable in ALL directions — Nazi racial nationalism is the archetypal evil §1.2). The 1935 Nuremberg Laws stripping citizenship, the blood-purity charts, Goebbels's propaganda apparatus, Kristallnacht Nov 1938. State the antisemitism as the foundational evil it was, building toward the Holocaust. Real, named, factual — the recognition skill is seeing how a state legislates a people out of humanity. No theatricalized reveal; the record is the argument.

topics.name: Gandhi and Indian independence movement
topics.scope: Nonviolence, Salt March, civil disobedience
topics.framing_note: Courage and a moral method shown by example (moral_vision §2). The 240-mile Salt March to the sea 1930, satyagraha, the spinning wheel, 'an eye for an eye leaves the whole world blind.' The named action is the answer. Present non-Western moral leadership on its own terms (framework Pillar 5 — NOT an exotic foil). Honest complexity available (the bank doesn't hagiograph) but the core is the genuine achievement of toppling an empire by moral force.

topics.name: Rise of militarist Japan
topics.scope: Manchuria 1931, expansion, Rape of Nanking
topics.framing_note: State the aggression and atrocity plainly (framework forbids sanitizing). The Mukden Incident 1931 (staged pretext), puppet Manchukuo, the League's impotence, the militarist takeover of the civilian government. CRITICAL: the Rape of Nanking 1937 (~200,000-300,000 killed, mass atrocity) must be stated as established fact, not euphemized (moral_vision §4) — see the injected decomposed topic. Honest about Asian aggression as the Pacific road to WWII. No condescension to Japan as a civilization (Pillar 5), but no soft-pedaling the war crimes.

topics.name: Policy of appeasement and Munich 1938
topics.scope: 'Peace for our time,' Sudetenland given away
topics.framing_note: The anti-totalitarian lesson the vision prizes (moral_vision §1.2): feeding an aggressor invites more aggression. Chamberlain's paper waved at Heston aerodrome, 'peace for our time,' the Sudetenland handed over, Churchill's 'you were given the choice between war and dishonour; you chose dishonour and you will have war.' Named specifics are answers. Present Chamberlain's case at its strongest (a war-weary nation, unready military) — moral_vision §6 no strawman — then the verdict history rendered, stated as fact.

topics.name: Aggression unchecked: Rhineland, Ethiopia, Anschluss
topics.scope: Dictators' moves the League ignored
topics.framing_note: The step-by-step slide as recognition-pattern (moral_vision §1.2 anti-totalitarian). Each named move is a cool-fact answer: the 1936 Rhineland remilitarization (Hitler's bluff with troops ordered to retreat if France resisted — France didn't), Mussolini's gas-and-bombs conquest of Ethiopia 1935-36 (Haile Selassie's League speech: 'It is us today; it will be you tomorrow'), the 1938 Anschluss. The pattern of unchecked aggression stated as historical fact, no editorializing needed — the record argues itself.

topics.name: Spanish Civil War
topics.scope: 1936 Franco, Guernica, dress rehearsal
topics.framing_note: The 'dress rehearsal' for WWII — German Condor Legion testing blitzkrieg, Soviet aid to the Republic. Guernica bombed April 1937, Picasso's mural as the named cool fact/answer. CRITICAL balance (moral_vision §6, §3.1): present this WITHOUT the romanticized pro-Republican-only frame common in textbooks — the Republican side included Soviet-directed NKVD purges of its own (Orwell's Homage to Catalonia documents the communist betrayal of the anarchists/POUM). Atrocities on BOTH sides stated as fact; no false hero/villain binary. Steelman the international-brigade idealism AND name the Stalinist manipulation of it.

topics.name: Nazi-Soviet Pact of 1939
topics.scope: Hitler-Stalin deal to carve Poland
topics.framing_note: Two totalitarian powers as PARTNERS, not opposites — a recognition the vision insists on (moral_vision §1.2, §3.1 — the bank does not let the USSR off as merely the later 'good ally'). The Aug 23 1939 Molotov-Ribbentrop pact and its SECRET PROTOCOL dividing Poland and the Baltics is the named cool fact/answer. The two regimes jointly invaded and partitioned Poland in Sept 1939; the USSR then annexed the Baltics and attacked Finland. State the Soviet aggression plainly — see injected Katyn topic. No 'forced marriage of convenience' apologetics for either side.

topics.name: Art and disillusionment after the war
topics.scope: Dada, Surrealism, the Lost Generation
topics.framing_note: Western cultural history (Pillar 1) presented on its own terms. How the slaughter shattered faith in progress and reshaped art: Dada's anti-art provocations (Duchamp's urinal 'Fountain' 1917), Surrealism (Dalí, the dream-logic), the Lost Generation writers (Hemingway, Remarque's All Quiet on the Western Front, Fitzgerald). The named work/movement is the answer. Present the disillusionment as a real intellectual response, neither celebrated nor scolded — the curious narrator.

topics.name: WWI poetry and remembrance
topics.scope: In Flanders Fields, the poppy
topics.framing_note: Western literary inheritance + memory (Pillar 1, moral_vision §2). McCrae's 'In Flanders Fields' and the poppy it created, Owen's 'Dulce et Decorum Est' (the gas attack, the bitter Latin), Sassoon, Brooke's 'some corner of a foreign field.' The named poem/line is the cool-fact answer. The poppy as the enduring symbol of remembrance — a sticky, dignified hook. Let the poetry's own weight carry it; no 'war is futile' gloss imposed.

topics.name: The Holodomor — Stalin's terror-famine in Ukraine
topics.scope: 1932-33 engineered famine, 3.5-7M dead, the Duranty cover-up
topics.framing_note: REQUIRED, decomposed from the consensus 'Rise of Stalin' lump because the framework names it explicitly and HEAVY. Count it honestly: collectivization tripled grain quotas, borders sealed so starving villagers couldn't flee, peasants caught gleaning dropped grain were shot, 3.5-7M Ukrainians dead. CRITICAL named figures (the cool-fact answers): Walter Duranty won the 1932 Pulitzer reporting it as 'exaggerated propaganda' while privately conceding to the British embassy 'perhaps 10 million' had died — Pulitzer never revoked; Gareth Jones broke the truth honestly and was murdered in Mongolia 1935. No false equivalence, no soft-pedaling; distractors include the establishment-minimized scale. This is the bank's signature truth-telling cell.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.1 and HISTORY_FRAMEWORK Pillar 4 name the Holodomor, the specific 3.5-7M toll, AND Walter Duranty's NYT cover-up by name as required content. The consensus list folds it invisibly into 'Five-Year Plans, purges' — the vision demands it stand as its own decomposed, named topic with the Duranty/Jones drama.

topics.name: Lenin's Red Terror and the founding of the Gulag
topics.scope: The Cheka, mass executions, and the labor-camp system from 1918
topics.framing_note: REQUIRED to correct the romantic 'Russian Revolution' frame. The terror did NOT begin with Stalin: Lenin's Cheka (Dzerzhinsky) launched the Red Terror in 1918, the Tambov rebellion was crushed with poison gas, hostage-taking and class-extermination decrees, and the first concentration camps (Solovki) date to 1918-1923. Solzhenitsyn's central thesis (the cool-fact answer): the Gulag was a CORE FEATURE of the Soviet state from its founding, designed not accidental — the camp system Stalin merely scaled. State the Bolshevik violence against peasants, priests, and rival socialists plainly (moral_vision §4 show-the-evil). Steelman nothing about the terror itself.
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK Pillar 4 explicitly requires 'the Gulag system founded 1918, not a Stalin aberration' and Solzhenitsyn's thesis that it was designed-not-accidental. moral_vision §3.1 cites the Gulag scope and the 1917-onward record. The consensus 'Russian Revolution of 1917' topic risks a heroic-Bolshevik frame; the vision requires the Leninist terror named at its true origin.

topics.name: Katyn and the Soviet invasion of Poland 1939-40
topics.scope: The other half of the Pact — 22,000 Polish officers murdered, the Baltic annexations, the Winter War
topics.framing_note: REQUIRED so the Nazi-Soviet Pact is not told as Germany's crime alone. When the USSR took its half of Poland in Sept 1939, the NKVD murdered ~22,000 Polish officers, police, and intelligentsia in the Katyn Forest (and other sites) spring 1940 — then blamed the Nazis for decades; the USSR admitted it only in 1990. The named atrocity (Katyn) is the cool-fact answer. Also: the forced annexation of Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania 1940 and the Winter War against Finland 1939-40. State Soviet aggression as established fact with no false equivalence (moral_vision §3.1) — the bank refuses to launder the USSR's 1939-41 record because it later joined the Allies.
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK Pillar 4 names 'Katyn Forest 22,000 Polish officers murdered' explicitly. moral_vision §3.1 requires honest accounting of communist killing with named perpetrators. The consensus covers the Pact only as a 'shocking deal to carve Poland' — the Soviet ATROCITIES that followed (Katyn, the Baltic seizures, the Winter War) are vision-mandated and absent.

topics.name: The Rape of Nanking
topics.scope: 1937 mass atrocity, ~200,000-300,000 killed
topics.framing_note: REQUIRED, decomposed from 'Rise of militarist Japan' because a mass atrocity of this scale must stand as its own named cell, not a clause. State plainly: over six weeks from Dec 1937, Japanese forces killed an estimated 200,000-300,000 Chinese civilians and prisoners in the captured Nationalist capital, with mass executions and systematic atrocity. The cool-fact answer hook (moral_vision §2 ordinary-courage-by-example): John Rabe, a German businessman and Nazi Party member, used his swastika armband's protective status to shelter ~250,000 Chinese in the Nanking Safety Zone — a startling case of one man's courage. Show the evil; honor the rescuer; no euphemism (framework forbids sanitizing).
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK forbids 'sanitizing... Aztec sacrifice / Plains torture' and by the same rule any mass atrocity; moral_vision §4 requires showing evil plainly. The consensus buries Nanking inside 'Rise of militarist Japan' as a parenthetical — an atrocity of this magnitude is vision-mandated to stand decomposed, with the John Rabe virtue-by-example hook the framework's voice rules favor.

topics.name: Interwar Western breakthroughs — the expanding universe and penicillin
topics.scope: Lemaître's Big Bang, Hubble, Fleming's 1928 accident, the dawn of modern physics
topics.framing_note: REQUIRED counterweight: the bank's HEAVIEST pillar (Western tradition as achievement) is nearly absent from the consensus interwar list, which is almost all war and dictatorship. The 1920s-30s were also a golden age of Western discovery. Cool-fact answers: Georges Lemaître — a Belgian Catholic PRIEST — proposed in 1927 what became the Big Bang (moral_vision §3.4: modern science largely the work of believers), confirmed by Hubble's 1929 redshift law; Alexander Fleming's accidental 1928 penicillin mould on a Petri dish (ordinary ingenuity, §2); the quantum revolution (Heisenberg's uncertainty 1927, the Solvay 1927 photograph of Einstein-Bohr-Curie). Wonder-first, the strange thing led. This restores the inheritance-worth-transmitting balance the strand otherwise loses.
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK names Pillar 1 (Western tradition unbroken — science, art, the great minds) as HEAVIEST and §7 'drama of the great minds across ALL tiers,' and moral_vision §3.4 specifically celebrates believing scientists (Lemaître named as Big Bang originator). The consensus interwar list is overwhelmingly war/atrocity/economics with almost no Western intellectual achievement — a vision-mandated imbalance to correct.

topics.name: Coolidge prosperity and the limited-government 1920s
topics.scope: The decade's real growth under low taxes and light regulation
topics.framing_note: REQUIRED so the American interwar story is not ONLY the New Deal expansion of government. Present as fact, not advocacy (moral_vision §6, no-verdict-on-contested): the 1920s saw real, broad-based prosperity, electrification, and the rise of the automobile and consumer economy under the Harding-Coolidge tax cuts (Mellon's rate reductions) and limited federal footprint. The named specific (Coolidge's 'the chief business of the American people is business'; the Mellon tax cuts) is the cool-fact answer. Balances the consensus's heavy New-Deal/positive-government tilt by making the limited-government, sound-money, dynamic-growth account of the era available — steelmanned, factual, not a sermon.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.3 (Austrian/limited-government coverage at least equal to interventionist accounts) and §3.6 (the dynamic American economy) require the limited-government prosperity case be present. The consensus interwar-America cells are the Crash, the Depression, and FDR's New Deal — all the government-expansion side; the vision mandates the other half (Coolidge-Mellon growth) be available, presented as fact.

topics.name: Appeasement and the Munich Agreement
topics.scope: Chamberlain, 'peace for our time', Sudetenland 1938
topics.framing_note: Steel-man the appeasers, then tell the truth (moral_vision §6): Chamberlain was not a fool but a man haunted by the Somme who genuinely believed he was sparing a generation. Present that sincerely, then state the result — the carve-up of a democracy emboldened the aggressor. Churchill's 'you were given the choice between war and dishonour; you chose dishonour and you will have war' belongs here as the named counter-voice.

topics.name: Invasion of Poland and Blitzkrieg
topics.scope: Sept 1 1939 war begins; lightning-war tactics
topics.framing_note: Story-led, the beauty-of-mechanism angle on the tactic (moral_vision §2): combined arms — Stukas, Panzers, radio — collapsing a defense that fought the last war. CRITICAL vision overlay: Poland was invaded from BOTH sides — Germany Sept 1, the Soviet Union Sept 17 under the secret pact. An Anglo-centric telling omits the eastern half; the bank does not (anti-totalitarianism in every form).

topics.name: Nazi-Soviet (Molotov-Ribbentrop) Pact
topics.scope: Aug 1939 Hitler-Stalin secret carve-up of Poland
topics.framing_note: VISION-LOAD-BEARING (moral_vision §1.2, §3.1; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK line 146 'honest about Soviet role'). The two totalitarian powers were collaborators before they were enemies — the secret protocol divided Poland, the Baltics, and Finland. State that Stalin's USSR was an active partner in starting the war in the East, supplied Germany with grain and oil until June 1941, and only 'switched sides' when invaded. No false equivalence-erasure that paints Stalin as a pure victim-ally from the start.

topics.name: Fall of France 1940
topics.scope: Six-week defeat, Maginot Line bypassed, occupation
topics.framing_note: Surprise-reversal energy (moral_vision §2): the strongest army in the West on paper collapsed in six weeks because doctrine, not courage, failed — the Ardennes 'impassable' to tanks. Present on its own terms; the drama of a great power's sudden fall is the hook. The human cost of occupation stated plainly without editorializing.

topics.name: Dunkirk Evacuation
topics.scope: 1940 'little ships' rescue 338,000 from beaches
topics.framing_note: Ordinary ingenuity + courage celebrated (moral_vision §2): fishing boats, pleasure yachts and lifeboats crewed by civilians crossing the Channel under fire to lift an army off the sand. This is virtue-through-example — show the deed, never preach it. 'Deliverance' was Churchill's own word; pair it with his warning that 'wars are not won by evacuations.'

topics.name: Battle of Britain
topics.scope: 1940 RAF vs Luftwaffe; radar; 'the Few'
topics.framing_note: Western tradition defending itself + beauty of mechanism (moral_vision §2, §3.3): the Dowding System — radar chain, plotting tables, ground control — as a real technological-organizational achievement, not just brave pilots. 'Never in the field of human conflict was so much owed by so many to so few' is the named quote. A free people holding the line alone against tyranny: celebrate it honestly.

topics.name: The Blitz
topics.scope: London bombed nightly 1940-41; civilian resilience
topics.framing_note: Courage under fire shown, not sentimentalized (moral_vision §5): the Underground shelters, St Paul's standing amid the smoke (the famous photograph), Coventry's cathedral gutted Nov 1940. Tell the home-front endurance straight. Avoid both jingoism and the cynical 'myth of the Blitz' debunking frame; state what people actually did.

topics.name: Winston Churchill's Wartime Leadership
topics.scope: 'Blood, toil, tears and sweat'; defiant speeches
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Euro; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Canonical Western moral-courage figure (moral_vision §2 'courage in pursuit of truth', §3.6). The voice that refused terms when surrender looked rational — 'we shall fight on the beaches', 'never surrender'. Celebrate the defiance and the oratory honestly. The bank may note he was a complex, flawed man (Gallipoli, his imperial views) without theatricalizing it — flawed humans who did extraordinary things, per the Founders rule applied generally.

topics.name: Battle of the Atlantic and U-Boats
topics.scope: Convoys vs wolfpacks; supply lifeline to Britain
topics.framing_note: Mechanism + ordinary endurance (moral_vision §2): the convoy system, sonar/ASDIC, escort carriers, and the merchant seamen who sailed knowing the odds. Churchill said the U-boat peril was the only thing that ever truly frightened him — use that. The codebreaking link (Ultra reading U-boat traffic) connects to Bletchley as a genuine science-wins-wars thread.

topics.name: North Africa and El Alamein
topics.scope: Rommel the 'Desert Fox' vs Montgomery, 1942 turn
topics.framing_note: Story-led generalship (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 3). Present Rommel on his own terms as a formidable and relatively chivalrous opponent (the desert war's reputation as a 'war without hate') — honest assessment, not demonization of every German soldier. Churchill: 'Before Alamein we never had a victory. After Alamein we never had a defeat.' The turning-point framing is the hook.

topics.name: Operation Barbarossa
topics.scope: 1941 German invasion of USSR; largest in history
topics.framing_note: Anti-totalitarianism in every form (moral_vision §1.2): two totalitarian empires now at war with each other. State the scale honestly AND its character — this was a war of annihilation and racial ideology, with the Einsatzgruppen following the front lines (the 'Holocaust by bullets'). The kid should see Hitler's fatal two-front gamble AND that the Eastern Front was the war's deadliest and most ideologically savage theater.

topics.name: Siege of Leningrad
topics.scope: 872-day blockade; ~1M dead; ice 'Road of Life'
topics.framing_note: Human endurance stated plainly (moral_vision §4 'honest, not preachy'). A starving city for 872 days, the frozen Lake Ladoga supply route, Shostakovich's Seventh Symphony performed by skeletal musicians and broadcast at the Germans. Celebrate the endurance of the people; the bank can honor Russian suffering and courage while never laundering Stalin's regime — the two are separable and the vision keeps them separate.

topics.name: Battle of Stalingrad
topics.scope: 1942-43 turning point; German 6th Army destroyed
topics.framing_note: The eastern hinge of the war, told straight (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 3). Honor the staggering courage and sacrifice of the soldiers and the city. Vision overlay: do NOT romanticize the Soviet command — Order No. 227 'Not One Step Back', blocking detachments shooting their own retreating men, are part of the honest record. Soviet soldiers fought heroically AND were driven by a murderous regime; both true.

topics.name: Battle of Kursk
topics.scope: 1943 largest tank battle; Soviets seize initiative
topics.framing_note: Mechanism + decisive-moment hook (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 3): the greatest clash of armor in history, Prokhorovka, the moment Germany permanently lost the initiative in the East. Present on its own terms — the technical drama of Tigers vs T-34s and the strategic consequence. Ultra intelligence's role in forewarning the Soviets is a fair codebreaking thread.

topics.name: Pearl Harbor
topics.scope: Dec 7 1941 surprise attack; 'day of infamy'
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US/World; Britannica
topics.framing_note: The American story (moral_vision §2, §3.6; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2). The attack that brought the United States into the war it would help win. FDR's 'a date which will live in infamy' is the named anchor. Tell it as the pivot that mobilized the arsenal of democracy. State plainly without the contested 'FDR knew' conspiracy framing (out of scope per the no-flame-bait rule).

topics.name: Bataan Death March
topics.scope: 1942 brutal forced march of POWs in Philippines
topics.framing_note: Atrocity stated as fact (moral_vision §4 'state what happened'). The brutal treatment of surrendered American and Filipino troops is part of the honest record of the Pacific war. No sensationalism, no condescension toward Japan-as-culture — state the specific conduct plainly, the way the bank states all atrocities.

topics.name: Doolittle Raid
topics.scope: 1942 first US bombers strike Tokyo off carriers
topics.framing_note: Daring + ingenuity celebrated (moral_vision §2): launching land bombers off a carrier deck, a one-way mission flown for morale when America needed hope. Virtue-through-deed. The strategic ripple (it helped push Japan toward the Midway gamble) is a satisfying mechanism payoff.

topics.name: Battle of the Coral Sea
topics.scope: 1942 first carrier battle; ships never saw each other
topics.framing_note: Beauty of mechanism / surprise-reversal (moral_vision §2): the first naval battle in history where the opposing fleets never sighted each other — warfare changed forever, decided by aircraft over the horizon. The wonder hook is the strangeness of the new kind of battle.

topics.name: Battle of Midway
topics.scope: June 1942 four Japanese carriers sunk; Pacific turn
topics.framing_note: The decisive Pacific turn, story-led (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 3). The codebreaking that set the ambush (Station Hypo cracking the 'AF' target), the five fatal minutes when American dive-bombers caught the carriers with planes on deck. Honest celebration of an American victory won by intelligence, courage, and a measure of luck — name all three.

topics.name: Guadalcanal Campaign
topics.scope: 1942-43 first US ground offensive in the Pacific
topics.framing_note: American story / endurance (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2): the grueling first land offensive, the naval battles off Savo Island, the Marines holding Henderson Field. Tell the slog straight as the start of the long road back. Present on its own terms.

topics.name: Island-Hopping Strategy
topics.scope: Leapfrogging Japanese strongholds toward the homeland
topics.framing_note: The winning American plan, mechanism-first (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2): bypassing fortified islands to let them 'wither on the vine' rather than assaulting each one. A clever strategic idea explained clearly — the kind of ordinary-genius-applied-at-scale the bank loves.

topics.name: Battle of Iwo Jima
topics.scope: 1945 brutal island fight; flag-raising photo
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US; Britannica
topics.framing_note: American courage, iconic image (moral_vision §2; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2). Rosenthal's flag-raising on Suribachi as a genuine cultural-canon photograph. 'Uncommon valor was a common virtue' — Nimitz's line — is virtue-through-example done for you. Honor the Marines' sacrifice; state the ferocity plainly.

topics.name: Battle of Okinawa
topics.scope: 1945 last great battle; kamikazes; mass casualties
topics.framing_note: Honest record of the Pacific endgame (moral_vision §4). The mass casualties — military and Okinawan civilian — and the kamikaze onslaught made this the bloody preview that directly shaped the atomic-bomb calculation. State the human cost plainly; this topic is the factual bridge to the Hiroshima decision, so the casualty reality must be concrete.

topics.name: Kamikaze Pilots
topics.scope: Japanese suicide-plane attacks on Allied ships
topics.framing_note: Present on its own terms, no condescension (moral_vision §4). Explain the tactic and the desperation behind it — a regime spending its young men as guided weapons — without exoticizing or mocking. The recognition skill is understanding how a militarist ideology demanded this; honest, not sensational.

topics.name: D-Day / Normandy Invasion
topics.scope: June 6 1944 largest seaborne invasion; Western front
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US/World; Britannica
topics.framing_note: The liberation of Western Europe — top-billing American/Allied story (moral_vision §2, §3.6; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2). The scale, the deception (Operation Fortitude), the Mulberry harbors, the bluffs of Omaha Beach, Eisenhower's pre-drafted note taking sole blame had it failed (a stunning act of integrity — use it). Celebrate the deed; honor the dead; state the cost.

topics.name: Liberation of Paris
topics.scope: Aug 1944 Paris freed; De Gaulle's return
topics.framing_note: Liberation moment told straight (moral_vision §2). The emotional reclaiming of an occupied capital, the role of the French Resistance and the Free French. Vision overlay: honor the Resistance as virtue-through-deed, but the bank does not airbrush the messier aftermath (the réglement de comptes) — state plainly if it comes up, without dwelling.

topics.name: Battle of the Bulge
topics.scope: 1944-45 last German offensive; 'Nuts!' at Bastogne
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US; Britannica
topics.framing_note: American story / courage at cost (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2). The surprise winter offensive, the surrounded 101st at Bastogne, McAuliffe's one-word reply 'Nuts!' to the German surrender demand — a named, kid-memorable moment. Vision overlay: the Malmedy massacre of American POWs is part of the honest record of this battle. Celebrate the stand; state the atrocity.

topics.name: Fall of Berlin and Hitler's Death
topics.scope: 1945 Soviet assault; Hitler's suicide in the bunker
topics.framing_note: The end of the Third Reich, stated plainly (moral_vision §4). Hitler's suicide in the bunker, the regime's collapse. Vision overlay (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK line 146 'honest about Soviet role'): the fall of Berlin also began the mass rapes and brutality of the Soviet occupation and the descent of the Iron Curtain over the East — the seed of the next moral conflict. Don't end the European story on a clean triumphalist note that hides what came next for half of Europe.

topics.name: Kristallnacht
topics.scope: 1938 'Night of Broken Glass' pogrom against Jews
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Euro; Holocaust curricula
topics.framing_note: Holocaust documented unflinchingly (moral_vision §4; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK line 146). The state-organized pogrom — synagogues burned, shops smashed, 30,000 Jewish men sent to camps — as the turn from legal persecution to open, organized violence. State it plainly. The recognition skill: how a regime escalated by stages, and how the world's silence registered.

topics.name: Nazi Ghettos (Warsaw Ghetto Uprising)
topics.scope: Jews walled into ghettos; 1943 Warsaw revolt
topics.framing_note: Courage at cost / virtue-through-deed (moral_vision §2, §4). The 1943 Warsaw Ghetto Uprising — starving, near-unarmed fighters holding off the SS for weeks, knowing they would lose — is one of history's purest acts of defiance. Honor it as such. State the confinement and the deportations plainly; the resistance is the wonder, the atrocity is the honest record. (Distinct from the 1944 Warsaw Rising of the Home Army — keep them separate.)

topics.name: The Final Solution and Wannsee Conference
topics.scope: 1942 bureaucratic plan to exterminate Europe's Jews
topics.framing_note: Anti-totalitarianism foundational (moral_vision §1.2, §4). The chilling fact the bank does NOT flinch from: genocide organized as cold bureaucracy — a 90-minute meeting over lunch where officials coordinated the murder of a continent's Jews. The 'banality of evil' recognition (Arendt) — that ordinary clerks administered mass murder — is the load-bearing lesson. State it plainly; no euphemism.

topics.name: Auschwitz and the Death Camps
topics.scope: Industrialized murder; gas chambers; ~6M Jews killed
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP World/Euro; Holocaust curricula
topics.framing_note: THE central fact, documented unflinchingly (moral_vision §4 'show the evil'; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK line 146). Industrialized murder of approximately six million Jews, plus Roma, Poles, Soviet POWs, the disabled, and others. State the scale and the method plainly — never sanitize, never theatricalize as a reveal. This is the bank's supreme example of where flinching from a hard topic is itself a failure.

topics.name: Anne Frank and the Diary
topics.scope: Hidden Jewish girl; diary in the Amsterdam annex
topics.framing_note: The human entry point (moral_vision §5 'children deserve moral formation'). One girl's voice makes six million comprehensible to a child. Story-led: the secret annex, the helpers who risked everything (Miep Gies hiding the diary), the betrayal, Bergen-Belsen. 'In spite of everything I still believe people are really good at heart' — handle with care, paired with the truth of what happened to her. The most accessible Holocaust topic for T1.

topics.name: Liberation of the Camps
topics.scope: 1945 Allied troops discover and free the camps
topics.framing_note: The moment the evidence became undeniable (moral_vision §4). Eisenhower ordering the atrocities filmed and German civilians marched through to see, specifically so no one could later deny it ('Get it all on record now... somewhere down the track of history some bastard will get up and say this never happened') — that act of deliberate documentation is the named, load-bearing detail. State what the soldiers found plainly.

topics.name: Righteous Rescuers (Schindler, Wallenberg)
topics.scope: Schindler's list; Wallenberg's passports save Jews
topics.framing_note: VISION-CENTRAL: virtue through example at cost (moral_vision §2, §4 'courage in pursuit of truth'). Individuals who chose to save lives when it was lethal to do so — Schindler bankrupting himself, Raoul Wallenberg issuing thousands of protective passports in Budapest then vanishing into Soviet captivity (note the second totalitarian swallowing the hero). The bank shows the deed and lets it speak. HIGH weight — this is exactly the moral formation the vision exists for.

topics.name: Enigma and Bletchley Park Codebreaking
topics.scope: Turing breaks German cipher; Ultra intelligence
topics.framing_note: Beauty of mechanism + drama of the great minds (moral_vision §2; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 6). Secret mathematics that shortened the war by an estimated two years and saved countless lives — Turing's bombe, the Poles (Rejewski) who cracked Enigma FIRST and gave their work to the Allies (an honest credit the popular telling drops). Turing's tragic postwar fate is part of the record, stated plainly, not theatricalized. The wonder is that abstract logic won battles.

topics.name: Navajo Code Talkers
topics.scope: Marines use Navajo language as unbreakable code
topics.framing_note: Ingenuity + honest American complexity (moral_vision §2, §3.7). Native Americans whose own language became an unbreakable battlefield cipher — celebrate the achievement and the men. The bank may note without editorializing that some had been punished as children for speaking that same language in government schools; honest history holds both, no theatrical irony.

topics.name: Manhattan Project
topics.scope: Secret US atomic bomb program; Oppenheimer; Trinity
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US/World; Britannica
topics.framing_note: American scientific achievement + moral weight (moral_vision §2, §3.6; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 6). The race to unlock the atom — Einstein's letter, Oppenheimer, the Trinity test, 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.' Present the genuine scientific feat AND the gravity. Vision-relevant thread: Soviet espionage (Klaus Fuchs, the Rosenbergs) penetrated the project — honest history that ties into the coming Cold War. Drama of minds at the breaking point.

topics.name: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
topics.scope: Aug 1945 atomic bombings end the war
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US/World; Britannica
topics.framing_note: Hard topic, honest not preachy (moral_vision §4). State the facts: the only wartime use of atomic weapons, the immediate and lingering deaths, and the genuine decision-context (Okinawa's casualty preview, the projected cost of invading Japan). Present the real moral argument on its own terms WITHOUT imposing a verdict — the bank states what happened and the competing considerations, and lets the player weigh them. No 'we now know better' framing; no glibness about the suffering (viral test).

topics.name: The American Home Front (Rosie the Riveter)
topics.scope: War production, rationing, women in factories
topics.framing_note: The arsenal of democracy (moral_vision §3.6; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2). The astonishing free-society production miracle — a continent retooling, Liberty ships built in days, women filling the factories. 'We Can Do It!' as cultural canon. Celebrate the mobilization of a free people honestly; the productive capacity of the American system is itself part of why fascism lost.

topics.name: Japanese-American Internment
topics.scope: 120,000 forced into camps; Korematsu case
topics.framing_note: American failure stated plainly, NOT theatricalized (moral_vision §3.6, §9 'not triumphalist'). This is explicitly on the vision's named list of American injustices to state as fact. 120,000 people, two-thirds citizens, imprisoned without charge; Korematsu (and the later coram nobis vacatur) as the civil-liberties failure. Pair honestly with the 442nd Regimental Combat Team — Japanese-American soldiers who became among the most decorated units in U.S. history while their families were behind wire. Both truths, no reveal-staging.

topics.name: Tuskegee Airmen
topics.scope: First Black US military pilots; escort record
topics.framing_note: Virtue-through-example against injustice at home (moral_vision §2, §3.7; named in the celebrate list, line 53). The first Black American military pilots, whose excellence — the bomber-escort record — was achieved while fighting segregation in their own country. Celebrate the achievement and the men; the injustice they overcame is stated as fact, part of the same honest American record. Civil-rights tradition as moral victory.

topics.name: European Resistance Movements
topics.scope: French Resistance, partisans, sabotage, spies
topics.framing_note: Ordinary courage under occupation (moral_vision §2, §4). Maquis, the SOE 'setting Europe ablaze', the Norwegian heavy-water sabotage at Vemork (a genuinely cinematic, true story that denied Hitler atomic material), the Danish rescue of nearly all its Jews by fishing boat. Virtue-through-deed. Honor the resisters specifically and by named operation rather than as a faceless category.

topics.name: Rape of Nanjing
topics.scope: 1937 Japanese atrocity in China; mass killing
topics.framing_note: Atrocity stated as fact, no flinching (moral_vision §4; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 5 honest-brutality discipline). The mass killing and rape in Nanjing 1937 is the Asian war's pre-1941 horror kids should not miss. Vision-aligned addition the consensus scope omits: John Rabe, the German businessman (and Nazi Party member) who led the Nanjing Safety Zone and sheltered ~200,000 Chinese — a complicated rescuer worth naming. State the atrocity plainly, no sensationalism, no anti-culture framing.

topics.name: Strategic Bombing and Tokyo Firebombing
topics.scope: Dresden and Tokyo raids; mass civilian deaths
topics.framing_note: Hard moral question presented WITHOUT a verdict (moral_vision §4, viral test). State the facts — the firebombing of Dresden, the March 1945 Tokyo raid that killed roughly 100,000 in one night. Present the genuine debate (military necessity vs the morality of area bombing of cities) on its own terms; do not impose 'we now know better,' and do not be glib about the dead. This is exactly the kind of contested-ethics topic the bank handles by stating, not preaching.

topics.name: Mussolini and Fascist Italy
topics.scope: Il Duce; fascism's origin; 1945 execution
topics.framing_note: Anti-totalitarianism in every form (moral_vision §1.2). The ORIGINAL fascist regime — define fascism as the actual historical ideology (corporatist, ultranationalist, anti-liberal) so the kid knows what the word genuinely means, not as a generic insult. Mussolini's march on Rome, the cult of Il Duce, the grim end at Lake Como 1945. Present the doctrine seriously enough to be recognized and rejected on the merits.

topics.name: The Big Three (Yalta and Potsdam)
topics.scope: Roosevelt, Churchill, Stalin plan the postwar world
topics.framing_note: VISION-LOAD-BEARING bridge to the Cold War (moral_vision §3.6; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK line 146 'honest about post-war carve-up', pillar 4). Yalta where the fate of Eastern Europe was effectively conceded to Stalin, and the betrayal of Poland — the nation whose invasion started the war handed to a new tyranny. State honestly that the defeat of one totalitarianism left half a continent under another. This seeds the Cold War as moral conflict; do not present Yalta as a clean diplomatic triumph.

topics.name: FDR's Wartime Leadership
topics.scope: Four-term president; Lend-Lease; 'arsenal of democracy'
topics.framing_note: American story, flawed-but-extraordinary leadership (moral_vision §3.6; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2, line 28 'flawed humans who built something extraordinary'). The president who marshaled the arsenal of democracy and Lend-Lease. Celebrate the wartime leadership honestly while not sanitizing — internment was signed by his hand (Executive Order 9066), and his trust of Stalin at Yalta is fairly questioned. Show the man, not the monument.

topics.name: Allied Commanders (Eisenhower, Patton, MacArthur)
topics.scope: Key US generals of Europe and the Pacific
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US; Britannica
topics.framing_note: Story-led generalship, real characters (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 3, pillar 6 drama). Eisenhower the coalition-holding statesman-general (and his D-Day integrity note); Patton the profane armored genius; MacArthur's 'I shall return.' Present them as the vivid, flawed, formidable personalities they were — the human drama is the hook, not a hagiography. Named moments and quotes are the memorable detail.

topics.name: V-E Day and V-J Day
topics.scope: May & Aug-Sept 1945 victory celebrations; surrenders
topics.source: Core Knowledge Gr8; AP US; Britannica
topics.framing_note: The victory of free peoples over tyranny, celebrated honestly (moral_vision §2). The formal surrenders (the deck of the USS Missouri for V-J Day), the jubilation. A legitimate moment of celebration in the bank — the defeat of fascism was a genuine good. Pair lightly with the sober truth that for Eastern Europe, one occupation simply replaced another (links to the Cold War strand without over-loading the celebration).

topics.name: Nuremberg Trials
topics.scope: 1945-46 Nazi leaders tried for crimes against humanity
topics.framing_note: The Western legal tradition applied to atrocity (moral_vision §3.4 rule of law, §3.6). The birth of the principle that 'I was following orders' is no defense and that leaders answer for crimes against humanity — a real achievement of the Anglo-American legal inheritance. Justice Jackson's opening is the named anchor. Honest-history footnote: the Soviet judges sat in judgment over crimes (Katyn) their own regime had committed — state plainly, no theatrical irony.

topics.name: Casualties and Scale of WWII
topics.scope: ~70-85M dead; deadliest conflict in history
