topics.framing_note: The human cost stated plainly, singular memorable framing (moral_vision §4; SHARED_PRINCIPLES single-number discipline). The deadliest conflict in human history. Vision overlay: be honest that the majority of the dead were civilians and that the USSR and China bore the largest losses — and that a large share of those Soviet deaths trace to Stalin's own conduct (purged officer corps, Order 227, deportations), not the Germans alone. The scale is the wonder; the honest accounting of who died and why is the discipline.

topics.name: The Katyn Forest Massacre
topics.scope: 1940 Soviet NKVD murder of ~22,000 Polish officers, police, and intelligentsia; the decades-long Soviet lie blaming the Nazis
topics.framing_note: VISION-REQUIRED, consensus-omitted. The framework explicitly names Katyn (line 106). This is the keystone WWII Soviet atrocity: the NKVD executed roughly 22,000 captured Polish officers and elites in 1940, then blamed Germany — a lie the USSR maintained until 1990 and the West partly tolerated for alliance convenience. Anti-totalitarianism in EVERY form (§1.2) demands this sit beside the Nazi atrocities; an Anglo-American consensus list that records only Axis crimes during WWII fails the vision. State the murder, the cover-up, and the Western complicity in the silence plainly.
topics.rationale: The framework names Katyn directly (line 106) and demands the Soviet role be told honestly (line 146); the consensus list records Nazi atrocities (Auschwitz, Wannsee, Kristallnacht) but zero Soviet wartime atrocities. The vision's foundational symmetric anti-totalitarianism (§1.2) requires both totalitarian killers be counted. This is the single largest omission in the strand.

topics.name: Soviet Mass Deportations and the Brutal Occupation of the East
topics.scope: NKVD deportation of Poles, Balts, and others to the Gulag 1939-41; the 1944-45 Red Army occupation — mass rape, looting, and fresh terror — as the front moved west
topics.framing_note: VISION-REQUIRED, consensus under-covered. The war in the East had TWO totalitarian occupiers. From 1939 the Soviets deported hundreds of thousands of Poles, Estonians, Latvians, and Lithuanians to Siberia and the Gulag; in 1944-45 the Red Army's advance brought mass rape (estimates in the hundreds of thousands to over a million women) and a new reign of terror. The consensus list shows the Nazi occupation's horrors but is silent on the Soviet half. State both occupations plainly, no false-equivalence-erasure — for Poland and the Baltics, liberation from Hitler was the start of a second tyranny.
topics.rationale: The framework (line 146) explicitly requires honesty about the Soviet role and the post-war carve-up; the consensus list's only Soviet entries are heroic (Stalingrad, Leningrad) or neutral (Big Three). The vision's symmetric anti-totalitarianism (§1.2) mandates the Soviet occupation's atrocities sit on the same plane as the Nazi ones.

topics.name: Christian and Student Resistance of Conscience (Bonhoeffer, the White Rose)
topics.scope: Dietrich Bonhoeffer and the Confessing Church; Hans and Sophie Scholl and the White Rose student leaflets; faith- and conscience-driven defiance of the regime from inside Germany
topics.framing_note: VISION-REQUIRED, consensus-omitted. The vision celebrates courage-at-cost and treats Christianity as a substantive moral-historical agent (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK line 147; moral_vision §2, §3.4). Bonhoeffer — the pastor who opposed Hitler from conscience, joined the resistance, and was hanged at Flossenbürg days before liberation; Sophie and Hans Scholl of the White Rose, guillotined at 21 and 24 for distributing anti-Nazi leaflets in Munich — are the bank's archetypal virtue-through-deed figures. The consensus list has external rescuers (Schindler/Wallenberg) but no internal German resistance of conscience and no faith dimension. Show the deed; let it speak; never preach it.
topics.rationale: The vision foregrounds moral courage at cost (§2) and Christian moral agency in history (§3.4; framework line 147); the consensus list omits internal German resistance of conscience entirely. Bonhoeffer and the Scholls are exactly the formative figures the framework's celebrate-list (Solzhenitsyn, Douglass, the monks copying through plague years) exists to feature.

topics.name: The Forgotten Allies of the East (Polish Pilots, Polish Codebreakers, the 1944 Warsaw Rising)
topics.scope: Polish 303 Squadron in the Battle of Britain; the Polish mathematicians who broke Enigma first; the 1944 Warsaw Rising and the Red Army's deliberate halt across the Vistula
topics.framing_note: VISION-REQUIRED, consensus under-covered. The Allies of the East are the war's most-betrayed heroes and the bank should name them. Polish 303 Squadron was the highest-scoring RAF fighter unit in the Battle of Britain; Polish mathematicians (Rejewski, Różycki, Zygalski) broke Enigma BEFORE Bletchley and handed the method to the Allies. The 1944 Warsaw Rising: the Home Army rose against the Germans while the Red Army sat across the river and deliberately let the Nazis annihilate the Polish resistance Stalin would otherwise have had to subjugate himself. Honor the courage; state the Soviet betrayal plainly. Anti-totalitarianism + virtue-through-deed in a single strand.
topics.rationale: The Western-centric consensus credits Bletchley and 'the Few' but drops the Polish contribution that underlay both, and omits the 1944 Warsaw Rising entirely — a story where Allied heroism and Soviet treachery stand side by side, exactly the honest-about-the-Soviet-role discipline the framework (line 146) demands. Distinct from the 1943 Ghetto Uprising already on the list.

topics.name: The Iron Curtain Descends (Origins of the Cold War from the Ashes)
topics.scope: The post-1945 Soviet imposition of communist regimes across Eastern Europe; Churchill's 1946 'Iron Curtain' speech at Fulton naming the new division of Europe
topics.framing_note: VISION-REQUIRED bridge; the consensus list stops too early. It ends WWII at V-J Day / Nuremberg as a clean Allied triumph. The vision (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 4, line 146) insists the war's true ending includes the descent of half of Europe into a SECOND tyranny — Soviet-installed regimes from Poland to Bulgaria — and Churchill at Fulton 1946: 'From Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the Continent.' Frame this as the seed of the Cold War as moral conflict. The defeat of fascism was a real good; it was not the end of totalitarianism in Europe. Keeps the WWII strand honest rather than triumphalist.
topics.rationale: The framework's stance (line 146) is explicit that the post-war carve-up must be told; the consensus list's terminal topics (V-E/V-J Day, Nuremberg) risk a triumphalist 'good war neatly won' ending that the vision's anti-totalitarianism (§1.2) and not-triumphalist rule (§9) forbid. The Iron Curtain is the load-bearing transition the consensus omits and the natural handoff to the Cold War strand.

strands.strand: The Cold War & the modern world

topics.name: Iron Curtain & Churchill's Fulton Speech
topics.scope: Churchill names the Soviet divide of Europe
topics.source: Core Knowledge CKHG; AP Euro postwar
topics.framing_note: Story-led: Churchill out of power, March 1946 Fulton Missouri, the phrase 'an iron curtain has descended across the Continent.' Present the divide as what it was — free West vs. Soviet-imposed captivity, not a neutral 'two blocs.' Stem carries the quote; answer is the named image. Churchill saw the totalitarian threat clearly when others wanted to trust Stalin.

topics.name: Truman Doctrine & Containment
topics.scope: US policy to contain communist expansion
topics.framing_note: Present as the strategic spine of 40 years of the moral conflict. Truman 1947, Greece and Turkey, Kennan's 'Long Telegram' and the 'X' article as the intellectual origin (T4-T5). Frame containment as resisting a regime the vision treats as genuinely oppressive — not 'American aggression.' Steelman both the policy and its critics (overreach) without false equivalence.

topics.name: Marshall Plan
topics.scope: US aid rebuilds postwar Western Europe
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Euro; AP World
topics.framing_note: Celebrate as American generosity and strategic wisdom — $13B rebuilt the free West and inoculated it against communism. Pairs with the §3.2 economic lens: market recovery vs. the command-economy stagnation behind the Curtain. The contrast (West rebuilt and prospered; the East stagnated) is honest history, the seen-vs-unseen made visible across a continent.

topics.name: Berlin Blockade & Airlift
topics.scope: West Berlin supplied entirely by air 1948-49
topics.framing_note: Wonder + virtue: a plane landing every ~45 seconds, 'candy bombers' (Gail Halvorsen, Operation Little Vittles) dropping sweets to children. Frame as the free world feeding a city Stalin tried to starve into submission — courage and ingenuity against coercion. The cool fact (the cadence, the candy parachutes) is the answer.

topics.name: NATO vs. Warsaw Pact
topics.scope: Rival military alliances split the world
topics.framing_note: Distinguish the two camps honestly: NATO a voluntary alliance of free nations; the Warsaw Pact the instrument by which Moscow held captive nations in line (it was Warsaw Pact tanks that crushed Hungary 1956 and Prague 1968). Not a symmetric 'both had alliances' framing — name what each actually did.

topics.name: Chinese Revolution & Mao 1949
topics.scope: Communists win China; Mao takes power
topics.framing_note: This is a gateway to the §3.1 atrocity record — do NOT let it end at '1949 Mao wins.' The stem sets the takeover; the heaviest content (Great Leap Forward 30-45M, Cultural Revolution) lives in its own injected ladder. Chang & Halliday's Mao is the cited scholarship. Honest count, named perpetrator, no romanticizing the revolution.

topics.name: Korean War & the 38th Parallel
topics.scope: Hot war splits Korea; UN forces fight
topics.framing_note: The first shooting war of the moral conflict. Inchon landing (MacArthur's gamble), the Chinese intervention, the stalemate at the 38th. Frame the outcome morally legible: South Korea became free and prosperous; the North a totalitarian prison state (sets up the injected NK-camps topic). The divided peninsula at night — lights vs. darkness — is the wonder hook.

topics.name: McCarthyism & the Red Scare
topics.scope: Hunt for communists inside America
topics.framing_note: DUAL COMMITMENT held sharply (this is the hard path the vision demands). McCarthyism is named in moral_vision §3.6 and §9 as a genuine American FAILURE — blacklists, ruined innocents, demagoguery — stated plainly, Army-McCarthy hearings, 'Have you no sense of decency?' AND it is also true that Soviet espionage was real (Venona decrypts, Hiss, the Rosenbergs passed atomic secrets). Teach the kid to hold both: the spies were real AND the witch-hunt was an injustice. No false equivalence in either direction.

topics.name: The Space Race & Sputnik
topics.scope: US-Soviet competition to reach space
topics.framing_note: Wonder-first. Sputnik's October 1957 beep heard on shortwave radios worldwide — the shock that a totalitarian rival had reached orbit first. Gagarin, then the American response. Frame as the free world mobilizing its open science to catch and surpass a closed one. The specific cool fact (the beeping signal, 'the night the sky changed') is the answer.

topics.name: Apollo 11 Moon Landing 1969
topics.scope: Americans first walk on the Moon
topics.framing_note: CELEBRATE — moral_vision §2 and §3.6 name landing humans on the Moon as a signature American achievement of the open society. 'One small step,' the 1202 alarm, Armstrong piloting past the boulder field with seconds of fuel. The free world won the race to the Moon. Wonder + American-experiment pillar both fire here. High billing.

topics.name: Cuban Revolution & Fidel Castro
topics.scope: Castro brings communism to Cuba 1959
topics.framing_note: Do not romanticize the revolution. Frame honestly: Castro's takeover brought a one-party state 90 miles from Florida, and the La Cabaña executions (injected separately) followed. Che Guevara presented as the executioner he was, not the t-shirt icon. The mass exile of Cubans (the rafts, Miami) is part of the record. Honest, not cynical — state what the regime did.

topics.name: Cuban Missile Crisis 1962
topics.scope: Thirteen days at brink of nuclear war
topics.framing_note: High drama, present straight — thirteen days, the U-2 photos, the quarantine line, Vasili Arkhipov's submarine veto (T5 wonder: one Soviet officer's 'no' may have stopped a nuclear launch). The closest the world came to nuclear war is a fact, not a thesis. Let the suspense carry it; the named decisive detail is the answer.

topics.name: Nuclear Arms Race & MAD
topics.scope: Hydrogen bombs, missiles, mutual destruction doctrine
topics.framing_note: Explain the grim logic of Mutual Assured Destruction as the mechanism it was — why two enemies each built world-ending arsenals (the beauty/horror of mechanism, §2). Connects to Sakharov (injected): the man who built the Soviet H-bomb then turned dissident against it. Tsar Bomba (50 megatons) as the staggering specific. No editorial hand-wringing — the facts carry the weight.

topics.name: The Berlin Wall Goes Up 1961
topics.scope: East Germany walls off West Berlin
topics.framing_note: Frame the wall correctly per §framework-line-16: it was built to keep people IN — a regime that must imprison its own citizens has confessed its nature. The barbed wire overnight in August 1961, families split mid-street, the first escapes and the first deaths (Peter Fechter bleeding at the wall). The Berlin Wall as an evil that needed breaking — stated as the bank's settled view of a totalitarian act, not 'a Cold War tension.'

topics.name: Berlin Wall & 'Tear Down This Wall'
topics.scope: Reagan's Brandenburg Gate challenge to Gorbachev
topics.framing_note: CELEBRATE explicitly — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4 names Reagan at Brandenburg June 12 1987 as a Cold War moral high point. His own staff cut the line repeatedly; he kept it. 'Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!' The quote IS the answer. Part of the Reagan-Thatcher-JP2 coalition the vision says to celebrate. The moral clarity is the point.

topics.name: Vietnam War
topics.scope: US fights communism in Southeast Asia
topics.framing_note: Present honestly and without either myth: a costly, divisive war fought to contain communism. State the real costs (58,000 American dead, the draft, the home-front division) AND the real stakes — what followed the US withdrawal was not peace but the Khmer Rouge killing fields next door and the boat-people exodus from a unified communist Vietnam. Honest, not cynical; no 'imperial aggression' framing, no jingoist whitewash. The consequence of withdrawal belongs in the record.

topics.name: Hungarian Revolution 1956
topics.scope: Soviet tanks crush a Hungarian uprising
topics.framing_note: A captive nation rising for freedom, crushed by Soviet tanks — exactly the moral conflict the vision foregrounds. Students at the radio station, the toppled Stalin statue (only the boots left), Imre Nagy executed, the West watching and not intervening. Frame the courage and the betrayal plainly. Sets the pattern the injected 'captive nations' thread completes.

topics.name: Prague Spring 1968
topics.scope: Czech reform crushed by Warsaw Pact tanks
topics.framing_note: 'Socialism with a human face' (Dubcek) rolled back by Warsaw Pact tanks — Jan Palach's self-immolation in protest is the searing specific. Connect forward to Havel (injected): the playwright-dissident this crackdown forged. Frame as another captive-nation rising betrayed — the system could not tolerate even reform from within.

topics.name: Decolonization of India 1947
topics.scope: Independence and Partition of British India
topics.framing_note: Honest both ways: the largest colony wins self-rule (a genuine good) AND Partition unleashed 1-2M deaths and the largest migration in history. State the violence plainly (§4 honest-not-cynical). Non-Western actors on their own terms — Nehru, Jinnah, the Radcliffe Line drawn in weeks. Not a morality play about the West; the human cost of the partition is the sober center.

topics.name: Gandhi & Nonviolent Independence
topics.scope: Salt March, civil disobedience against British rule
topics.framing_note: Virtue-by-example (§2, §5): the man who beat an empire without weapons. The Salt March to the sea (240 miles, picking up a handful of salt as defiance), satyagraha defined inline. Honest at T5: Gandhi's method worked AGAINST a Britain with a conscience and a free press — a candor the vision's intellectual seriousness invites without diminishing the achievement. The named act (the salt) is the answer.

topics.name: African Decolonization & Ghana 1957
topics.scope: African nations win independence from Europe
topics.framing_note: Non-Western self-rule on its own terms (§framework pillar 6) — Nkrumah, Ghana first in 1957, the 'wind of change.' Present honestly, neither romanticized nor cynical: real liberation, and the hard road of building states afterward. Avoid both colonial-apologia and the inverse anti-Western condemnation framing (§9). The independence moment is the wonder; the named first nation is the answer.

topics.name: Suez Crisis 1956
topics.scope: Egypt nationalizes canal; Britain's power wanes
topics.framing_note: The moment the old empires lost the world stage — Britain and France humiliated when the US refused to back them, the torch passing to the two superpowers. Present as the structural shift it was (T4-T5 analyst register). Nasser, the canal, the Eisenhower pressure. No editorializing; the geopolitical reveal is the substance.

topics.name: Apartheid & Nelson Mandela
topics.scope: South African racial system and its fall
topics.framing_note: Racism against any group is morally unacceptable (§3.7) — apartheid stated plainly as the injustice it was. Mandela: 27 years on Robben Island, then president; the Rugby World Cup 1995 reconciliation gesture as virtue-by-example. Frame the fall as a moral victory AND honor Mandela's choice of reconciliation over revenge — the harder, nobler path. The specific (27 years; the number on his prison block) is the answer.

topics.name: Korean & Berlin Spy Drama / Espionage
topics.scope: Spies, U-2 incident, Rosenbergs, defectors
topics.framing_note: The secret war — wonder-rich. Powers' U-2 shot down 1960 (and the poison pin he didn't use), the Glienicke 'Bridge of Spies' exchanges, Kim Philby and the Cambridge Five. On the Rosenbergs, follow §3.6/McCarthy dual-commitment honesty: Venona decrypts later confirmed Julius's guilt — the espionage was real. Named figure or named operation is the answer; no fabricated tradecraft.

topics.name: Gorbachev: Glasnost & Perestroika
topics.scope: Soviet reforms of openness and restructuring
topics.framing_note: The reforms that accidentally unraveled the USSR — present the irony straight: a system that could not survive even partial honesty (glasnost) about itself. Define both terms inline. Frame within the moral conflict: the Western pressure (Reagan's arms buildup, the economic exhaustion per §3.2) is WHY reform became necessary — Gorbachev did not act in a vacuum. Honest about him as a reformer-Communist, not a liberator by intent.

topics.name: Solidarity & the Polish Workers' Movement
topics.scope: Walesa's union cracks communism in Poland
topics.framing_note: CELEBRATE — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4 names Solidarity, Walesa, and JP2 as heroes of the Cold War. The Gdansk shipyard strike, Walesa the electrician climbing the fence, 10 million members, martial law 1981, then victory in the 1989 elections. CRITICAL: pair with JP2's June 1979 Warsaw homily ('Be not afraid') as the spark — that linkage is explicitly vision-mandated. Workers and a pope toppled a regime. The named spark/figure is the answer.

topics.name: Fall of the Berlin Wall 1989
topics.scope: Crowds open the wall; East-West reunite
topics.framing_note: The night the evil that needed breaking finally fell (§framework-line-16). November 9 1989 — Schabowski's bungled press conference ('immediately, without delay'), crowds swarming Checkpoint Charlie, the hammers and the wall-peckers. CELEBRATE without restraint: this is the moral conflict's triumphant payoff. The specific (the accidental announcement that opened the gates) is the answer. High billing, accessible from T1.

topics.name: Collapse of the Soviet Union 1991
topics.scope: USSR dissolves into independent states
topics.framing_note: A superpower vanishes — December 25 1991, the red flag lowered over the Kremlin for the last time, the failed August coup, Yeltsin on the tank. Frame as the moral conflict's verdict: the open society outlasted the closed one, the West bankrupted the USSR (economic-exhaustion thread, §3.2). Not 'a tragedy,' not gloating — the empire that built the Gulag ended. The named final image is the answer.

topics.name: Tiananmen Square 1989
topics.scope: China crushes pro-democracy protest; Tank Man
topics.framing_note: Explicitly in the §3.1 atrocity record AND HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 ('Tiananmen Square June 4 1989 + Tank Man'). One man, the grocery bags, the column of tanks — the frozen image is the answer. State the crackdown plainly: the regime massacred its own citizens demanding freedom. Honest, unflinching; the courage and the brutality both stated as fact. Vision-mandated, high.

topics.name: Soviet War in Afghanistan
topics.scope: USSR's costly decade-long invasion and defeat
topics.framing_note: The 'Soviet Vietnam' that drained the empire — present as a contributing cause of the collapse (ties to the economic-exhaustion thread). The mujahideen, the Stinger missiles, 15,000 Soviet dead, the 1989 withdrawal. Honest at T5 about the long downstream consequences without dragging in post-2010 current politics (§6 dated-references line). The defeat that helped break the USSR is the substance.

topics.name: Founding of the United Nations 1945
topics.scope: Postwar body to keep world peace
topics.framing_note: Present on its own terms — the world's attempt to prevent another world war, San Francisco 1945, the Security Council and the veto. Honest, not idealized: the veto meant the USSR could block action, and the UN watched Hungary 1956 and Prague 1968 without stopping the tanks. State what it was designed to do and where the structure limited it. No advocacy either for or against.

topics.name: Creation of Israel 1948
topics.scope: Jewish state founded; Arab-Israeli conflict begins
topics.framing_note: Present straight as historical fact (T4-T5): the founding May 1948 in the shadow of the Holocaust, Ben-Gurion's declaration, the immediate war. CRITICAL per §6 dated-references + §framework current-politics line: keep it HISTORICAL — the 1948 founding and 1967/1973 wars are in scope; the present-day conflict and active politicians are OUT. No verdict on the contested present (§no-verdict-on-contested). State the founding and the conflict's origin as facts.

topics.name: Marshall-era Economic Miracles (Japan & West Germany)
topics.scope: Defeated nations become economic powerhouses
topics.framing_note: A natural §3.2/§3.3 economics-lens topic: how the LOSERS of WWII grew rich and FREE under market economies + the rule of law, while command economies stagnated. The German Wirtschaftswunder (Erhard freeing prices overnight 1948), Japan's rise. Frame as the seen-vs-unseen verdict made visible — free markets + sound institutions produced the miracle. The named reform/figure is the answer.

topics.name: Globalization & the Internet Age
topics.scope: Connected world economy, trade, and technology
topics.framing_note: §3.6 names the Internet as part of the technological substrate the American open society built. Frame the post-Cold-War connected world with the §3.2 trade lens (specialization and exchange lift billions out of poverty — a real human good). Keep it timeless and substantive (ARPANET origins, the container ship, the fall of trade barriers); steer clear of post-2010 current-politics flashpoints (§6).

topics.name: September 11, 2001
topics.scope: Terror attacks reshape the modern era
topics.framing_note: In scope (the framework permits settled events through ~2010; 9/11 is historical fact, not active partisan debate). Present soberly and concretely — the towers, the hijacked planes, Flight 93's passengers fighting back ('Let's roll') as virtue-by-example under the §4 honest-not-cynical rule. Keep STRICTLY to the 2001 event and its immediate human story; do NOT drift into post-2010 war-on-terror politics (§6). The named act of courage is the answer; glib distractors banned (§viral 'glib about real suffering').

topics.name: European Union & the Euro
topics.scope: Former enemies unite into one economic bloc
topics.framing_note: Present on its own terms — old rivals (France and Germany, three wars in 70 years) building a single market and currency, a genuine achievement of postwar peace. Honest at T5 with the §3.2 lens available: monetary union without fiscal union has real tensions worth naming as economics, not partisanship. Keep timeless; no post-2010 current-politics (§6). No verdict — present the structure and the aspiration.

topics.name: The Holodomor & Walter Duranty's Cover-Up
topics.scope: Stalin's engineered Ukrainian famine 1932-33 and the NYT reporter who hid it
topics.framing_note: MANDATED in the heaviest detail the bank possesses. 3.5-7M Ukrainians; collectivization tripled grain quotas; borders sealed; villagers caught eating dropped grain shot. Walter Duranty's NYT cover-up EXPLICITLY NAMED — won the 1932 Pulitzer for whitewash reporting while privately conceding to the British embassy 'perhaps 10 million' had died; Pulitzer never revoked. Gareth Jones broke the story honestly and was murdered in Mongolia 1935 (virtue-at-cost). Steelman distractors include the establishment-soft-pedaled 'about half a million' so the kid picks the honest number. The consensus list folds the entire USSR into 'glasnost' and 'collapse' — the atrocity record MUST stand on its own.
topics.rationale: The single most vision-mandated topic of this strand and entirely absent from the consensus list. moral_vision §3.1 and HISTORY_FRAMEWORK Pillar 4 + §3 name the Holodomor with specific tolls AND name Duranty's cover-up by name — not optional emphasis but required content.

topics.name: Mao's Great Leap Forward & Cultural Revolution
topics.scope: The largest famine in history and the decade of chaos that followed
topics.framing_note: MANDATED. Great Leap Forward 1958-62: 30-45M dead (the largest famine in human history); backyard furnaces melting farm tools for useless pig-iron; the four-pests campaign (killing sparrows → locust plagues); grain exported during famine. Cultural Revolution 1966-76: Red Guards, the 'four olds,' intellectuals sent to the countryside, struggle sessions. Chang & Halliday's Mao cited. The consensus 'Chinese Revolution 1949' entry stops at the takeover; the atrocities — the actual human cost of Maoism — are required content the consensus list omits entirely.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.1 and HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 name the Great Leap (30-45M) and Cultural Revolution explicitly with tolls. The consensus list covers Mao taking power but NOT what his regime did to its own people — exactly the 'communist atrocities decomposed' the overlay instruction calls for.

topics.name: The Khmer Rouge & the Killing Fields
topics.scope: Pol Pot's Year Zero and the Cambodian genocide 1975-79
topics.framing_note: MANDATED. 2M dead (a quarter of Cambodia's population); Year Zero; the forced evacuation of Phnom Penh at gunpoint; people killed for wearing glasses (a mark of the educated); Tuol Sleng / S-21 prison; the Killing Fields. State the evil plainly (§4). CRITICAL linkage the bank should make: this followed the US withdrawal from Indochina — the consequence-of-withdrawal thread noted on the Vietnam topic. Honest, unflinching, no euphemism.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.1 and HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 name the Khmer Rouge (2M, Year Zero, Tuol Sleng, Killing Fields) explicitly. The consensus list has no Cambodia entry at all — a decomposed communist atrocity the vision requires.

topics.name: The Gulag & Solzhenitsyn's Witness
topics.scope: The Soviet camp system and the man who exposed it from inside
topics.framing_note: MANDATED at the highest billing — Solzhenitsyn is a named exemplar in moral_vision §2, §4, §5, AND §8 (one of only four 'great question' models). The Gulag Archipelago built from 227 prisoner testimonies, ~18M passed through the camps; Magadan, Kolyma, Vorkuta. The VIRTUE story is the heart: he memorized fragments and smuggled them out chapter by chapter, never holding the full manuscript, because the KGB would find it. Arrested 1945, One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich 1962, exiled 1974. Show virtue by example (§5), never preach it. The book proved the camps were a CORE FEATURE of the Soviet state from 1918, not a Stalin aberration.
topics.rationale: Solzhenitsyn is the single most-cited individual exemplar across moral_vision (§2, §4, §5, §8) and a Cold War hero named in HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4. The consensus list does not mention the Gulag or Solzhenitsyn at all — an omission the vision treats as non-negotiable required content.

topics.name: Sakharov, Havel & the Dissidents of Conscience
topics.scope: The scientists and writers who defied the Soviet bloc from within
topics.framing_note: MANDATED — moral_vision names Sakharov and Havel directly (§1 lineage 'the moral witness of Solzhenitsyn, Havel, and Sakharov'; §2 virtue exemplars). Andrei Sakharov: built the Soviet H-bomb, then lost everything (the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize he couldn't collect, internal exile in Gorky) opposing the regime's weapons and lies. Vaclav Havel: the playwright jailed for samizdat, typing under occupation, who walked from prison cell to the presidency of a free Czechoslovakia (the Velvet Revolution 1989). Courage-at-cost (§2, §5) — show it, don't preach it. These are the human faces of the moral conflict's victory.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §1 explicitly names 'the moral witness of Solzhenitsyn, Havel, and Sakharov' as part of the bank's intellectual lineage, and §2 lists both as virtue exemplars. The consensus list has Gorbachev's reforms and the Wall falling but NONE of the heroes of conscience the vision foregrounds — a required injection.

topics.name: North Korea: The Prison State
topics.scope: The totalitarian regime and camps that still operate
topics.framing_note: MANDATED. moral_vision §3.1 names 'North Korean prison camps that still operate' as part of the established atrocity record; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 names the kwan-li-so camps and the Arduous March famine (hundreds of thousands to millions dead, 1990s). The night-time satellite photo (South ablaze with light, North a black void) is the wonder-legible hook and the answer. Frame as the still-living proof of what the Korean War's northern outcome produced — the consensus 'Korean War' entry stops at 1953; the regime's nature is the required completion. Keep historical (the famine, the camp system as documented) without drifting into active current-politics (§6).
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.1 explicitly names North Korean camps 'that still operate'; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 names the kwan-li-so and Arduous March. The consensus list covers the Korean War but not the totalitarian state it left behind — a vision-mandated decomposition of an ongoing communist atrocity.

topics.name: Castro's Cuba: La Cabaña & the Exiles
topics.scope: The executions and exodus that followed the Cuban Revolution
topics.framing_note: MANDATED. HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 names 'Castro's La Cabaña executions; Che killed Bolivia 1967.' The consensus 'Cuban Revolution & Castro' entry presents the takeover but not what the regime DID: Che Guevara presiding over the La Cabaña firing squads, the political prisoners, the mass exodus (the 1980 Mariel boatlift, the rafters). Present honestly (§4) — this punctures the romantic-revolutionary myth with the documented record. The named place/figure is the answer.
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §3 explicitly names La Cabaña and Che's executions as required atrocity-record content. The consensus list covers Castro's rise but soft-pedals the regime's repression — exactly the decomposition the overlay demands, and a correction to the t-shirt-icon framing.

topics.name: Reagan's 'Evil Empire' & the Coalition That Won the Cold War
topics.scope: The Reagan-Thatcher-John Paul II partnership and the moral case against the USSR
topics.framing_note: MANDATED to CELEBRATE — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4 names 'the Reagan-Thatcher-John Paul II coalition celebrated' and 'Reagan's 1983 Evil Empire speech' specifically. Reagan named the USSR what it was when détente-minded elites called it gauche; the arms buildup (and SDI/'Star Wars') that the §3.2 economic-exhaustion thread says helped bankrupt the Soviets; Thatcher the 'Iron Lady'; JP2 the Polish pope. Frame as the moral-clarity-plus-strategy that ended the conflict. This is the Cold War's moral spine and the consensus list reduces Reagan to one wall speech.
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4 explicitly names the Reagan-Thatcher-JP2 coalition AND the 'Evil Empire' speech as celebrated, mandated content. The consensus list has 'Tear Down This Wall' but not the broader coalition or the moral case — the vision treats this strategic-moral partnership as the heart of how the Cold War was won.

topics.name: John Paul II's Warsaw Homily: 'Be Not Afraid'
topics.scope: The 1979 Mass that sparked Solidarity and shook the Soviet bloc
topics.framing_note: MANDATED — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4 names 'JP2's June 1979 Warsaw homily (Be not afraid) as the spark of Solidarity' specifically. The Polish pope returning home June 1979; a million Poles in Victory Square chanting 'We want God'; the regime watching its monopoly on public life evaporate in nine days. Treat Christianity as the substantive historical force it was (moral_vision §3.4, framework 'stance preserved') — JP2 as a real Cold War agent, not decoration. The named phrase is the answer. Pairs directly with the Solidarity topic.
topics.rationale: HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §4 explicitly names the June 1979 Warsaw homily and 'Be not afraid' as the spark of Solidarity — required, celebrated content. The consensus list omits JP2 entirely despite naming Solidarity; the vision insists on Christianity-in-history as a substantive force and names this exact moment.

topics.name: The Civil Rights Movement as Moral Victory
topics.scope: Douglass-to-King and the natural-rights case that ended Jim Crow
topics.framing_note: MANDATED at the bank's core. moral_vision §3.6 and §8 name the natural-rights line 'Frederick Douglass at Rochester (1852), Abraham Lincoln at Cooper Union (1860), Martin Luther King in Birmingham (1963)' — and the Douglass July-4th question is one of only FOUR 'great question' exemplars in §8. The KEY framing: the movement WON by appealing to the natural-rights tradition of the founding documents (King's 'promissory note,' the Letter from Birmingham Jail), not by rejecting them — America's failure measured against America's own creed. State Jim Crow plainly (§3.6 named failure). Virtue-by-example. The home-front moral story of the modern American era; the foreign-policy-weighted consensus list has no purely-American civil-rights entry.
topics.rationale: The Douglass/Lincoln/King natural-rights line is named in moral_vision §1, §3.6, AND §8 (a 'great question' model), and HISTORY_FRAMEWORK Pillar 2 calls the civil rights movement a 'moral victory.' Foundational American-story content for the modern era that the foreign-policy-weighted consensus list omits — a required injection per the overlay's 'American founding deepened / Western-tradition achievements' instruction.

topics.name: The Economic Verdict: How the West Bankrupted the USSR
topics.scope: Why the command economy lost — the calculation problem made visible
topics.framing_note: MANDATED by the bank's economics spine. moral_vision §3.2-§3.3 treat the Mises-Hayek calculation problem as established fact — and the Cold War was the largest real-world test of it. Frame the Soviet collapse not as bad luck but as the PREDICTED result: without market prices for capital goods, the planners could not rationally allocate; chronic shortages, the bread queues, the empty shelves beside a bristling arsenal. The seen-vs-unseen (§3.2 Bastiat lens) made continental. Steelman the planned-economy case at its strongest, then let the historical result answer it (moral_vision steelmanning rule). This connects the Cold War's end to WHY it ended on the terms it did.
topics.rationale: moral_vision §3.2 and §3.3 elevate the economic calculation problem to established-fact status and say command-economy questions should 'cite the calculation problem the way questions about gravity cite Newton.' The Cold War's economic dimension — why central planning lost — is the vision's signature intellectual claim, and the consensus list treats the collapse as purely political with no economic-cause content.

topics.name: Archimedes of Syracuse
topics.scope: Ancient Greek inventor and mathematician
topics.framing_note: Lead with the wonder + the courage-unto-death drama, not the formula. 'Don't disturb my circles' as his last words at the Roman sack of Syracuse 212 BC (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK names this as a T1 drama-of-minds hook); the bath-tub Eureka; the lever ('give me a place to stand'); the screw still lifting water; the war machines that held off Rome. Founding genius of the Western mechanical tradition (moral_vision §3.3 Athens lineage). The cool specific is the answer, not Archimedes' name.

topics.name: Aristotle as natural philosopher
topics.scope: Classical observation, classification, geocentric model
topics.source: AP World; Core Knowledge; Western tradition canon
topics.framing_note: NO condescension toward the past (moral_vision §4): 'Aristotle was not stupid for thinking the heart was the seat of thought.' Present him as the man who taught the West to OBSERVE and CLASSIFY — the marine-biology dissections, the systematic study of animals — whose authority then shaped 2000 years. The reversal hook is that his very greatness made his errors load-bearing (the thing Galileo/Copernicus had to overturn was Aristotle-via-the-Church-authority). Athens node of the Athens-to-Philadelphia inheritance (§3.3).

topics.name: Ptolemy and the geocentric universe
topics.scope: Earth-centered model dominant until Copernicus
topics.framing_note: Present on its own terms — the geocentric model was a genuine predictive achievement (epicycles forecast planetary positions for 1400 years), not a dumb superstition. Frames the Copernican revolution: you can't feel the drama of Copernicus/Galileo without respecting what they had to dethrone. Beauty-of-mechanism angle (§2): WHY the model worked well enough to last.

topics.name: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
topics.scope: Calculated Earth's circumference with shadows
topics.framing_note: Pure wonder + ordinary ingenuity (moral_vision §2): a librarian in Alexandria measured the whole planet with two sticks, two shadows, and the distance between Syene and Alexandria — and got it nearly right ~240 BC. Surprise-reversal payload: educated ancients KNEW the Earth was round and roughly how big (kills the flat-earth-myth misconception). The decidable cool fact (how he did it / what shadow angle) is the answer.

topics.name: Roman engineering: aqueducts, roads, concrete
topics.scope: Aqueducts, roads, arches, Roman concrete
topics.source: AP World; Core Knowledge Rome unit
topics.framing_note: Beauty-of-mechanism (§2: 'WHY the Roman concrete still stands') + the Rome node of the Western inheritance (§3.3). The self-healing seawater concrete, the Pont du Gard, the gravity-fed aqueduct gradient, roads still walkable 2000 years on. Western art + architecture as inheritance worth celebrating (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK). The specific marvel (Pantheon's unreinforced dome, the concrete chemistry) is the answer.

topics.name: Chinese Four Great Inventions
topics.scope: Paper, printing, gunpowder, the compass
topics.source: AP World; Core Knowledge China units
topics.framing_note: Non-Western civilization on its OWN terms, NOT an exotic foil (moral_vision §4, HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 5). Song-dynasty printing, the lodestone compass, gunpowder from alchemists seeking immortality. Honest comparison without condescension AND without false equivalence: China invented these first, yet the institutional take-off happened in the West (§4 'some traditions developed institutions others did not... the bank says so when relevant'). The specific origin/use is the answer.

topics.name: Islamic Golden Age: algebra, optics, medicine
topics.scope: Al-Khwarizmi, Ibn al-Haytham, Avicenna, House of Wisdom
topics.framing_note: Covered substantively but NOT over-weighted (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 5 explicit). Ibn al-Haytham inventing the controlled experiment in optics; al-Khwarizmi's algebra; Ibn Sina's Canon as the medical text for 600 years; the Baghdad House of Wisdom translation movement. Courage-in-pursuit-of-truth roster names Ibn Sina (§2). The honest DECLINE thread is REQUIRED here and I inject it separately (al-Ghazali ~1100, Mongol sack of Baghdad 1258) — stated as historical fact, not editorialized.

topics.name: Hindu-Arabic numerals and zero
topics.scope: Place-value system and the concept of zero
topics.framing_note: Wonder + non-Western achievement on its own terms: zero as a number (Brahmagupta's rules ~628), place value, the system that traveled India to Baghdad to Fibonacci's Pisa. The reversal: Roman numerals make arithmetic almost impossible — the 'nothing' symbol was a revolution. Concrete-over-abstract (§5): why you can't multiply MMXLVIII easily. The specific innovation is the answer.

topics.name: Isaac Newton: gravity and motion
topics.scope: Gravity, three laws, Principia, calculus, prism
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Euro; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: The supreme Scientific-Revolution figure and explicitly a BELIEVER (moral_vision §3.4 names Newton; HISTORY_FRAMEWORK 'Newton, Galileo, Kepler — all believers per the historical record'). The plague-year 1666 apple at Woolsthorpe is a T1 drama hook. Unified heavens and Earth under one physics. The prism splitting white light, the inverse-square law, the three laws — the specific marvel is the answer. The Newton-Leibniz priority dispute is a T3 drama hook (note: calculus belongs to the math strand).

topics.name: Leeuwenhoek, Hooke and the microscope
topics.scope: Microscope reveals cells and microbes
topics.framing_note: Pure wonder — opening the unseen world (§2 'Octopuses see with their skin'-style strangeness). A Delft cloth-merchant grinding his own lenses saw 'animalcules' swimming in pond water and his own tooth scrapings; Hooke's Micrographia drew the flea and coined 'cell' from monastery cells. Ordinary ingenuity (§2). The specific first-sighting is the answer.

topics.name: Columbus and the voyages of 1492
topics.scope: Atlantic crossing, Spain, the Americas
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US/World; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Honest, not cynical, not preachy (moral_vision §4 — uses THIS exact case): 'The Columbian Exchange caused devastating Indigenous mortality from disease — state it. Don't editorialize.' Tell the navigation/seamanship marvel AND the demographic catastrophe plainly, no theatrical reveal, no 'we now know better.' Kill the flat-earth myth (educated people knew the Earth was round; the real dispute was its SIZE — Columbus was wrong, he thought it small). The specific is the answer.

topics.name: Vasco da Gama and the sea route to India
topics.scope: Rounded Africa to reach India, 1498
topics.source: AP World; Core Knowledge Age of Exploration
topics.framing_note: Age of Exploration on its own terms — the ocean spice route that broke the Venetian/overland monopoly and reoriented world trade. Honest about the violence da Gama brought to the Indian Ocean (not theatricalized, just stated). The specific navigational/geographic feat (rounding the Cape, the monsoon-wind crossing) is the answer.

topics.name: Prince Henry, the caravel and navigation tools
topics.scope: Caravel, astrolabe, compass, Portuguese exploration
topics.source: AP World; Core Knowledge Age of Exploration
topics.framing_note: Beauty-of-mechanism + ordinary ingenuity (§2): the ships and instruments that made open-ocean voyaging possible. The lateen sail letting a caravel tack against the wind, the astrolabe/quadrant fixing latitude by the sun and Polaris, dead reckoning. The specific tool-and-what-it-solved is the answer. (Note: 'Henry the Navigator' himself rarely sailed — a teach-the-real-story angle, no hagiography.)

topics.name: Lewis and Clark expedition
topics.scope: Crossed America to the Pacific, Sacagawea
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: American story (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 2) + exploration wonder. Jefferson's Corps of Discovery mapping the Louisiana Purchase; Sacagawea as guide and interpreter (present her substantively, on her own terms, not as a token). The specific (the keelboat, the grizzly encounters, reaching the Pacific 'Ocian in view! O! the joy', the species catalogued) is the answer.

topics.name: Industrial Revolution: textiles and the factory
topics.scope: Spinning jenny, power loom, factory system
topics.framing_note: Real human progress stated honestly INCLUDING the human cost — but the economic substance is an Austrian/seen-unseen matter that lives in economics; here keep it to the inventions + their world-changing scale (§3.3 lens noted, not warped in). The reversal the bank can teach: industrialization, for all its grim early factories, is what ENDED mass subsistence poverty (Pinker/Enlightenment-Now data, §3.5). The specific machine-and-what-it-did is the answer.

topics.name: The steam locomotive and railroads
topics.scope: Stephenson's Rocket, transcontinental railroad
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US/World; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Wonder + American story: rail shrank a continent. Stephenson's Rocket winning the Rainhill Trials 1829; the Golden Spike at Promontory 1869 joining the transcontinental line. Honest about who built it (Chinese and Irish labor at brutal cost — stated plainly, §4). The specific (the Rocket's speed, the Spike, the gauge) is the answer.

topics.name: Eli Whitney: cotton gin and interchangeable parts
topics.scope: Cotton gin and interchangeable-parts manufacturing
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Honest history without theatrical reveal (§4, HISTORY_FRAMEWORK forbids sanitizing slavery): the cotton gin is the dark-irony case — a labor-saving invention that made short-staple cotton profitable and thereby ENTRENCHED and EXPANDED slavery rather than ending it. State the consequence plainly, no editorializing. The interchangeable-parts idea seeded mass production. The specific mechanism/consequence is the answer.

topics.name: Samuel Morse and the telegraph
topics.scope: Telegraph and Morse code, instant messages
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: First instant long-distance communication — annihilating distance is the wonder. 'What hath God wrought' as the first message 1844 (a real quote, biblical, fits the bank's matter-of-fact treatment of the era's faith, §3.4). The specific (the dot-dash code, the first-message content, the 1858 transatlantic cable) is the answer.

topics.name: Alexander Graham Bell and the telephone
topics.scope: Invented the telephone, 1876
topics.framing_note: Wonder of voice across wires. Honest teach-the-real-story: Bell beat Elisha Gray to the patent office by hours, and the work grew from teaching the deaf (his mother and wife were deaf). 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you' as the first call. The specific is the answer. No hagiography — the priority race is part of the honest record.

topics.name: Thomas Edison and the light bulb
topics.scope: Light bulb, phonograph, Menlo Park lab
topics.framing_note: American ingenuity (§2 ordinary ingenuity, §3.6 American technological substrate). Teach the REAL story, not the myth: Edison didn't invent the bulb, he found a carbon filament that lasted and built the whole electrical SYSTEM (generation, wiring, meters) around it — the 'invention factory' at Menlo Park was itself the innovation. The specific (the 1300 filament trials, the phonograph as his favorite, the system not the bulb) is the answer.

topics.name: The electricity pioneers: Faraday, Tesla, Franklin
topics.scope: Franklin's kite, Faraday's induction, Tesla's AC
topics.framing_note: Faraday is NAMED in moral_vision §3.4 as one of the believer-scientists ('Newton, Boyle, Faraday, Maxwell') — frame his self-taught bookbinder's-apprentice rise + deep Christian faith as virtue-by-example, NOT as incidental. Franklin's kite + the American-Founder-as-scientist angle (§3.6). Tesla's AC vs Edison's DC 'War of the Currents' drama. The specific discovery (induction = moving magnet makes current; Franklin proving lightning is electricity) is the answer.

topics.name: Louis Pasteur: germ theory and vaccines
topics.scope: Germ theory, pasteurization, rabies vaccine
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Euro; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: HISTORY-of-science achievement told STRAIGHT as the conquest of disease — proved germs (not 'bad air') cause illness; saved countless lives. IMPORTANT scope line: the institutional-capture/'trust the science' vaccine SCRUTINY (moral_vision §3.8, MEMORY vaccine-stance) is a SCIENCE-SUBJECT overlay, NOT this history topic — do not import that frame here. Here: the swan-neck flask killing spontaneous generation, the rabies-vaccine save of Joseph Meister 1885. The specific experiment is the answer.

topics.name: Darwin and evolution by natural selection
topics.scope: Beagle voyage, Galapagos, Origin of Species
topics.source: AP World/Bio; Core Knowledge; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Present the science straight + the discovery DRAMA (§2): the 5-year Beagle voyage, the Galapagos finch beaks, the 20-year delay until Wallace's letter forced his hand 1858, Origin 1859. NO science-vs-religion strawman either direction (§4 'no smug atheist voice'). Frame as the mechanism that reframed all living things; keep human-application/eugenics OUT (that scrutiny is a science-subject overlay per §3.7 and the science-bank eugenics-history line). The specific mechanism is the answer.

topics.name: Mendel and the foundations of genetics
topics.scope: Pea-plant experiments reveal heredity
topics.framing_note: Mendel is NAMED in moral_vision §3.4 as a believer-scientist ('Mendel, Lemaitre') — frame as the AUGUSTINIAN FRIAR in his monastery garden whose 8 years of pea-counting were IGNORED until rediscovered in 1900, 16 years after he died. Virtue by example (patient honest work unrewarded in his lifetime) + science-and-faith-not-opponents (§3.4). The specific (dominant/recessive ratios, the 3:1, why peas) is the answer.

topics.name: Joseph Lister and antiseptic surgery
topics.scope: Antiseptics make surgery survivable
topics.framing_note: Real human progress + courage against an establishment that mocked him (virtue by example, §2). Carbolic-acid antisepsis after he read Pasteur; surgeons resisted hand-washing for years (the Semmelweis-adjacent tragedy). The reversal: before this, surgery itself killed you via infection. The specific (carbolic spray, the germ-link, the death-rate collapse) is the answer.

topics.name: Fleming and the discovery of penicillin
topics.scope: Accidental mold discovery, first antibiotic
topics.framing_note: Wonder + ordinary ingenuity + surprise (§2): a contaminated petri dish in 1928 because Fleming was a messy housekeeper. Teach the REAL fuller story (the bank prizes precision): Fleming discovered it but Florey and Chain at Oxford a decade later turned it into a usable drug that saved WWII soldiers — the discovery alone wasn't enough. The specific (the mold-killing-bacteria observation; who made it a drug) is the answer.

topics.name: Roentgen and the X-ray
topics.scope: Discovered X-rays; first medical imaging
topics.framing_note: Pure wonder + surprise-reversal (§2): an accidental glow in a darkened lab 1895, then the eerie image of his wife's hand-bones-and-wedding-ring — the first time anyone saw inside a living body. He called them 'X' for unknown and refused to patent them (virtue: gave the gift freely). First Nobel in Physics. The specific (what he saw, why 'X', the hand image) is the answer.

topics.name: Marie Curie and radioactivity
topics.scope: Radium, polonium, two Nobel Prizes
topics.framing_note: Courage-in-pursuit-of-truth + virtue by example (§2, §4): a woman barred from French universities who processed TONS of pitchblende in a leaky shed to isolate radium, won TWO Nobels in different sciences, and ultimately died of the radiation she discovered. Frame her achievement on the merits (not as identity-tokenism — the bank rejects that, §3.5). The specific (polonium named for Poland, the glowing test tubes, two-Nobel feat) is the answer.

topics.name: The Wright brothers and powered flight
topics.scope: First airplane flight, Kitty Hawk 1903
topics.framing_note: NAMED THREE TIMES in moral_vision (§2 wonder, §2 courage, §2 virtue-by-example: 'the Wright brothers risking everything on a calculation,' 'staking everything on flight'). Two bicycle mechanics who built their own wind tunnel, solved 3-axis control when funded experts failed, and flew 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk 1903 — American ingenuity (§3.6 'the airplane' as American technological substrate). The specific (wing-warping/3-axis control, the wind tunnel, 12 seconds/120 feet) is the answer.

topics.name: Henry Ford and the assembly line
topics.scope: Model T, assembly line, mass production
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: American story + real human progress (§3.6): the moving assembly line cut a car from 12 hours to 90 minutes and the $5 day let workers buy what they built. Honest record (the bank doesn't hagiograph): Ford's later antisemitism is part of the factual record, stated plainly if relevant, never theatricalized (§4, HISTORY_FRAMEWORK no-hagiography rule). The specific (moving line, Model T, $5 day, 'any color so long as black') is the answer.

topics.name: The automobile and the internal combustion engine
topics.scope: Benz, Daimler invent the gasoline car
topics.framing_note: Beauty-of-mechanism (§2): the engine that put the world on wheels. Karl Benz's 1885 Patent-Motorwagen; Bertha Benz's unauthorized 1888 long-distance drive that proved the car worked (a great real-person wonder hook, told on her own terms). The specific (four-stroke cycle, who built the first practical car, Bertha's drive) is the answer.

topics.name: Einstein and relativity
topics.scope: Relativity, E=mc2, the famous physicist
topics.framing_note: Wonder at its purest (§2: 'Light bends around stars' is a moral_vision exemplar line — that IS the 1919 eclipse confirmation of general relativity). The patent-clerk who reimagined space and time in his 1905 'miracle year'; the bending-starlight test that made him world-famous overnight. Concrete handles over jargon (§5): the twin paradox, the train thought experiment. The specific (what bends, E=mc2 meaning, the 1919 eclipse) is the answer.

topics.name: The atomic bomb and the Manhattan Project
topics.scope: Splitting the atom, Oppenheimer, Trinity test
topics.source: AP US/World; Core Knowledge; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Hard topic handled HONESTLY, not preachy (§4): state the science and the stakes plainly — no theatrical 'was it a war crime' reveal, no glibness about the suffering (viral test, §7). Oppenheimer's 'Now I am become Death' (a real quote), the Trinity flash, Fermi's Chicago pile. American-led, ended the war. The specific (fission chain reaction, Trinity, the Oppenheimer quote) is the answer. The moral weight is carried by facts, not editorializing.

topics.name: Marconi, radio and broadcasting
topics.scope: Wireless radio, then television
topics.framing_note: Wonder of signals through empty air into every home. Teach the real contested story precisely (the bank prizes accuracy): Marconi sent the first transatlantic signal 1901, but Tesla's prior patents were later recognized — a genuine priority dispute, stated as fact. The specific (transatlantic 'S' in Morse, the priority question, the leap to broadcasting) is the answer.

topics.name: Polar exploration: Amundsen, Peary, Shackleton
topics.scope: Race to the South and North Poles
topics.framing_note: Courage + endurance as virtue-by-example (§2). Shackleton's Endurance crushed by ice, the 800-mile open-boat journey to South Georgia, and EVERY man brought home alive — leadership at the breaking point. Amundsen beating Scott to the South Pole 1911 (and Scott's whole party dying on the return). The specific (Shackleton's boat journey, Amundsen's dogs-vs-Scott's-ponies decision) is the answer.

topics.name: Everest: Hillary and Tenzing
topics.scope: First to summit Mount Everest, 1953
topics.framing_note: Wonder + the partnership: a New Zealand beekeeper and a Sherpa mountaineer reached the highest point on Earth 1953. Tell it on EQUAL terms — Tenzing as a full partner, not a porter (no condescension, §4); they agreed never to say who stepped first. The specific (the summit, the gracious shared-credit detail, the South Col route) is the answer.

topics.name: Sputnik and the start of the Space Age
topics.scope: First satellite, 1957, Space Race begins
topics.source: AP US/World; Core Knowledge; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: Cold War as moral conflict frame available (HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 4 / moral_vision §3.4): the beeping Soviet satellite that shocked America into the Space Race — the contest between a free society and a totalitarian one (which the free society won by landing on the Moon). State plainly that the Soviet program ran on prison-camp/coerced labor where relevant (§3.1, honest record). The specific (first artificial satellite, the beep, what it triggered) is the answer.

topics.name: Yuri Gagarin: first human in space
topics.scope: First person to orbit Earth, 1961
topics.framing_note: Wonder of the first human beyond the atmosphere 1961 — credit the achievement straight, on its own terms (no condescension toward the Soviet feat; honest history credits real accomplishment, §4). 'Poyekhali!' ('Let's go!'). The specific (first to orbit, single orbit ~108 min, his exclamation) is the answer. Pair-able with Sputnik/Apollo as the Space-Race arc.

topics.name: Apollo 11 and the Moon landing
topics.scope: Armstrong, Aldrin, 'one small step,' 1969
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP US; cultural-literacy canon
topics.framing_note: NAMED in moral_vision §3.6 ('put humans on the Moon') as a peak of the American experiment AND §2 American technological achievement. The peak of exploration — celebrate it fully and honestly. The 1202 alarm, Armstrong taking manual control with seconds of fuel left, 'the Eagle has landed,' 'one small step.' The specific (the landing drama, the quote, 400,000 people who built it) is the answer. Free society reaching the Moon = the Space-Race payoff.

topics.name: Watson, Crick, Franklin and the DNA double helix
topics.scope: Discovery of DNA's structure, 1953
topics.framing_note: Rosalind Franklin is NAMED in moral_vision §2 virtue-by-example — the recognition-justice angle is VISION-MANDATED, not optional. Her Photo 51 X-ray crystallography was the key evidence Watson and Crick used (shown to them without her knowledge); she died at 37 before the 1962 Nobel, which can't be awarded posthumously. Frame as the discovery of life's code AND honest about the credit (stated as fact, no theatrical reveal, §4). The specific (the double helix, base-pairing, Photo 51's role) is the answer.

topics.name: The computer pioneers: Babbage, Lovelace, Turing
topics.scope: Analytical engine, first programmer, Turing machine
topics.framing_note: Ideas behind modern computing + drama-of-minds (§2, HISTORY_FRAMEWORK 'Turing's apple' is a T4 hook). Babbage's never-built Analytical Engine; Ada Lovelace writing the first algorithm a century early (credit on the merits); Turing's universal machine, his Bletchley codebreaking that shortened WWII, and his tragic persecution and death — stated plainly, not theatricalized (§4). The specific (Lovelace's algorithm, the Turing machine concept, Enigma) is the answer.

topics.name: The transistor and the digital revolution
topics.scope: Transistor, microchip, personal computer
topics.framing_note: American technological substrate (moral_vision §3.6 names 'the integrated circuit'). The 1947 Bell Labs transistor (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley) → Kilby/Noyce's integrated circuit → the chip that built the modern world. Beauty-of-mechanism: the tiny switch replacing the hot fragile vacuum tube. The specific (what the transistor does, where it was invented, the IC leap) is the answer.

topics.name: The Internet and the World Wide Web
topics.scope: ARPANET, Berners-Lee invents the Web
topics.framing_note: American technological substrate (moral_vision §3.6 names 'the Internet'). Teach the real precision the bank demands: the INTERNET (ARPANET 1969, packet-switching, TCP/IP) and the WEB (Berners-Lee at CERN 1989-91, who gave it away free, no patent — virtue) are DIFFERENT things kids conflate. The specific (packet-switching vs the Web, the first message 'LO', Berners-Lee's free gift) is the answer.

topics.name: Mary Anning, the fossil hunter of Lyme Regis
topics.scope: Self-taught girl who found the first ichthyosaur and plesiosaur skeletons; supplied the science men published under their own names
topics.framing_note: VISION-MANDATED INJECTION — moral_vision §2 names her TWICE as the controlling virtue-by-example: 'Mary Anning earning a man's recognition from a girl's beach' and among 'people who told the truth at cost.' A poor working-class girl who survived a lightning strike as a baby, hunted fossils in the crumbling Lyme Regis cliffs to feed her family, found the first complete ichthyosaur at 12 and the first plesiosaur — and watched gentleman geologists publish her finds without crediting her, barred from the Geological Society because she was a woman. Wonder + courage + virtue + honest record of who got credit. The specific find/fact is the answer.
topics.rationale: The consensus list has ZERO paleontology and ZERO Mary Anning despite her being the single most-named virtue-by-example figure in the entire moral vision, and named specifically for this strand. Her omission is the largest vision gap here.

topics.name: Lemaitre, the priest who proposed the Big Bang
topics.scope: Belgian Catholic priest and physicist who first proposed the expanding universe and the 'primeval atom'
topics.framing_note: VISION-MANDATED INJECTION — moral_vision §3.4 names Lemaitre explicitly as the capstone of the believer-scientists list ('Lemaitre, who proposed what became the Big Bang') and as proof the bank 'does not treat science and Christianity as opponents.' Georges Lemaitre, a Catholic PRIEST, derived the expanding universe from Einstein's equations in 1927 and proposed the 'primeval atom' — and Einstein first told him 'your math is correct but your physics is abominable,' then recanted. Hubble's data confirmed the expansion. The reversal hook: the Big Bang's father wore a cassock. The specific (expanding universe / primeval atom / Einstein's reversal) is the answer.
topics.rationale: The consensus list jumps from Einstein straight to the atomic bomb with NO cosmology, omitting the one figure moral_vision §3.4 names as the load-bearing example of its 'science and Christianity are not opponents' thesis. Required to make that vision pillar land in this strand.

topics.name: Tycho Brahe and the war on the data
topics.scope: The naked-eye astronomer whose two decades of precise observations made Kepler's laws possible
topics.framing_note: VISION-MANDATED INJECTION — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §7 'Drama of the great minds' names 'Tycho's silver nose' as a canonical drama hook, and the strand currently runs the astronomy-revolution arc (Copernicus-Kepler-Newton) WITHOUT the man whose 20 years of pre-telescope naked-eye data were the empirical bedrock Kepler stood on. The Danish nobleman with a metal nose (lost in a duel over a math dispute), his island observatory Uraniborg, his pet elk, his strange death — and the priceless Mars data Kepler inherited. The specific (the silver/brass nose, the precision data, what Kepler did with it) is the answer. Wonder + drama-of-minds.
topics.rationale: The strand's astronomy ladder skips the observational-data link between Copernicus's idea and Kepler's laws; the framework explicitly flags Tycho as a drama-of-minds keystone for this exact era. Closes a named gap.

topics.name: The decline of the Islamic Golden Age: al-Ghazali and the sack of Baghdad 1258
topics.scope: How the medieval Islamic scientific flourishing ended — al-Ghazali's anti-rationalist turn and the Mongol destruction of Baghdad's House of Wisdom
topics.framing_note: VISION-MANDATED INJECTION — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK pillar 5 states the decline thread is REQUIRED honest history: 'al-Ghazali's Incoherence of the Philosophers (~1100) helped close the golden age's rationalist tradition; Mongol destruction of Baghdad 1258 ended the House of Wisdom... The pattern (religious orthodoxy stifling inquiry) is stated as historical fact, not editorialized.' The consensus 'Islamic Golden Age' topic covers the rise but NOT the fall. State plainly, no condescension, no triumphalism (§4): the Tigris ran black with ink from books thrown in the river 1258; why the recovery the West achieved didn't happen here. The specific cause/event is the answer.
topics.rationale: The consensus list covers the Islamic Golden Age's rise but omits the fall, which the framework explicitly REQUIRES as honest history and as the contrast explaining why the Scientific Revolution happened in the West. Without it the coverage is one-sided in the direction the vision forbids.

topics.name: Lise Meitner and the discovery of nuclear fission
topics.scope: The physicist who explained fission and was passed over for the 1944 Nobel that went to her collaborator
topics.framing_note: VISION-MANDATED INJECTION — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §7 names 'Lise Meitner overlooked at the 1944 Nobel' as a canonical T5 drama-of-minds hook, and she is the missing scientific link AHEAD of the Manhattan Project topic: it was Meitner (a Jewish physicist who had just fled Nazi Germany) and her nephew Frisch who first explained and NAMED nuclear fission in 1938, while her collaborator Otto Hahn alone got the 1944 Chemistry Nobel. Frame the recognition-justice as fact, not theatrical reveal (§4). The specific (she explained/named fission; the Nobel that omitted her; element 109 meitnerium named for her) is the answer.
topics.rationale: The strand has the Manhattan Project but not the fission discovery that made it possible, and the framework explicitly flags Meitner as a drama-of-minds keystone. A second vision-named woman-in-science whose recognition story the vision mandates.

topics.name: Boltzmann, entropy, and the equation on the tombstone
topics.scope: The physicist who founded statistical mechanics, fought for the reality of atoms, and whose entropy formula is carved on his grave
topics.framing_note: LOWER-PRIORITY VISION INJECTION — HISTORY_FRAMEWORK §7 names 'Boltzmann's tombstone S = k log W' as a canonical drama-of-minds hook. Ludwig Boltzmann statistically explained why heat flows one way (entropy), was ridiculed by colleagues who denied atoms even existed, and the formula they fought over is engraved above his name. Beauty-of-mechanism (§2) + drama-of-minds at the breaking point. The specific (entropy = why time has a direction; the tombstone equation) is the answer. Lower weight than the women-in-science injections — include if the strand wants a physics-foundations drama beat.
topics.rationale: Named in the framework's drama-of-minds roster for this strand; fills the thermodynamics/statistical-mechanics gap between the Industrial Revolution and modern physics. Lower priority than Anning/Lemaitre/Meitner.

topics.name: Parthenon and the Greek architectural orders
topics.scope: Athens Acropolis temple; Doric/Ionic/Corinthian
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Art History anchor work; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Top-billing Pillar-1 Athens keystone — the inheritance, not a museum label. Per the Wonder Pattern, ask for the cool specific (Phidias' colossal Athena, the entasis curve that has NO straight lines so it reads straight, the marbles painted in bright color not white), never 'name the order' rote. Frame as the template every later Western column descends from. Drama-available: if the stem invokes the Persian sack of the Acropolis, the answer is the rebuilt temple's trick, not a date.

topics.name: Roman Pantheon and the concrete dome
topics.scope: Hadrian's domed temple; oculus; lost concrete
topics.source: AP Art History; Core Knowledge ancient Rome
topics.framing_note: Pillar-1 Rome keystone explicitly named in framework ('Pantheon's still-standing concrete dome'). Celebrate the beauty of mechanism (moral_vision §2): WHY it still stands — the recipe (volcanic pozzolana, lighter aggregate up top), the lost formula that left it unmatched for 1,300 years until Brunelleschi. The oculus + rain-drain holes is the kid hook. This is the same lost-knowledge thread that sets up Brunelleschi.

topics.name: Gothic cathedrals (Chartres / Notre-Dame)
topics.scope: pointed arch, flying buttress, rose windows, stained glass
topics.source: Core Knowledge medieval; AP Euro; AP Art History
topics.framing_note: CORE of moral_vision §3.4 — medieval cathedrals as the monastic/ecclesiastical achievement that built the modern world, faith and engineering reaching toward light. NO smug 'people used to believe' voice (§4). Framework names Chartres rose windows + the Madonna's Veil relic, Sainte-Chapelle. Cool-fact answers: the flying buttress that lets walls become glass; Chartres' surviving medieval blue. Notre-Dame's 2019 fire + restoration is in scope (settled, not partisan) and a vivid hook.

topics.name: Brunelleschi's dome of Florence
topics.scope: 1436 Santa Maria del Fiore; herringbone brick; no scaffold
topics.framing_note: THE canonical worked exemplar of the whole bank (HISTORY_TEMPLATES §1) — one figure, five tier questions. Highest weight. Each cool fact gets its own answer: lost-Roman-formula (T1), herringbone (T2), the egg demonstration + 'you could have built my dome too' (T3), goldsmith-by-training (T4), still the largest masonry dome (T5). Engineering-feat-that-launched-the-Renaissance framing. NEVER stuff all five into one stem.

topics.name: St. Peter's Basilica and the Renaissance/Baroque papal Rome
topics.scope: Bramante/Michelangelo dome; Bernini's colonnade
topics.source: AP Euro; AP Art History; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Pillar-1 Renaissance-into-Baroque keystone. Celebrate the ambition straight; Christian heritage as historical foundation, not advertised (§4, no smug-believer voice). Cool-fact answers: Michelangelo taking over the dome in his 70s for free 'for the love of God'; Bernini's colonnade as 'the arms of the Church embracing the faithful' (his own image). Bramante nicknamed 'Maestro Ruinante' for demolishing old St. Peter's is a vivid hook.

topics.name: Leonardo da Vinci — Mona Lisa and Last Supper
topics.scope: sfumato; vanishing-point Supper; the Renaissance polymath
topics.source: Core Knowledge grade 5 Renaissance; AP Art History; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Archetypal Renaissance genius — Pillar-1 high weight + 'drama of the great minds' (Pillar 6). Cool-fact answers over rote: the mirror-writing notebooks; the Last Supper painted in failing experimental tempera so it began flaking in his lifetime; sfumato = 'smoke,' no visible lines. The polymath wonder (flying machines, anatomy dissections) is the §2 'ordinary ingenuity' lead. Avoid 'who painted' rote.

topics.name: Michelangelo — Sistine ceiling and David
topics.scope: 4-year ceiling; Creation of Adam; 17-foot David
topics.source: Core Knowledge grade 5; AP Art History; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Framework explicitly names 'Michelangelo's Sistine ceiling + David.' High weight. Drama-of-the-mind hooks: he insisted he was a sculptor not a painter and resented the ceiling commission; the David carved from a 'ruined' block other sculptors had abandoned; the near-touching fingers of Adam and God. Ask for the specific, not 'who sculpted David.'

topics.name: Raphael — School of Athens
topics.scope: Vatican fresco gathering all Greek philosophers
topics.source: AP Art History; AP Euro; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Perfect Pillar-1 synthesis — the Vatican itself honoring the Athens-to-Rome philosophical inheritance the bank champions (Athens→Jerusalem→Rome lineage). Cool-fact answer: Plato points up (the Forms) while Aristotle gestures down (the world) — the whole argument of Western philosophy in two hands; Raphael painted Leonardo's face onto Plato and slipped his own face into the crowd.

topics.name: Donatello and Ghiberti — early Renaissance sculpture
topics.scope: first freestanding nude David; Gates of Paradise
topics.source: AP Art History; Core Knowledge Renaissance
topics.framing_note: Framework names both ('Ghiberti's Gates of Paradise, Donatello's David — first freestanding nude since antiquity'). The revival-of-classical-antiquity thread of Pillar 1. Cool-fact answer: Donatello's bronze David was the first free-standing nude statue cast since the Romans, a thousand-year gap; Michelangelo reportedly named Ghiberti's doors the 'Gates of Paradise.'

topics.name: Botticelli — Birth of Venus and Primavera
topics.scope: Medici Florence; mythological subjects revived
topics.framing_note: Pillar-1 Medici-Florence keystone — the rebirth of classical mythology as subject matter. Present on its own terms. Cool-fact hook: Venus standing on a scallop shell as the first large mythological nude of the Renaissance; the Medici patronage that funded it. Avoid 'who painted' rote — ask the wondrous specific.

topics.name: Jan van Eyck and the Northern Renaissance
topics.scope: Arnolfini Portrait; oil-paint innovation; minute detail
topics.framing_note: Pillar-1 Northern thread — ordinary ingenuity (moral_vision §2): the oil-paint technique that let the North out-detail Italian fresco. Cool-fact answer: the convex mirror in the Arnolfini Portrait reflecting the whole room AND two figures in the doorway, with 'Jan van Eyck was here' signed above it like a witness. Mechanism-of-the-medium wonder, not attribution.

topics.name: Albrecht Durer — Northern Renaissance printmaking
topics.scope: engravings; self-portraits; Praying Hands
topics.framing_note: Where the print revolution (Gutenberg thread) meets Renaissance draftsmanship — ideas-strand crossover. Cool-fact hook: Durer's 1500 self-portrait deliberately composed to look like the traditional image of Christ (a statement about the artist as creator); his rhino woodcut drawn from a description he never saw in person, yet it shaped how Europe pictured rhinos for centuries. Present straight, no theatrical reveal.

topics.name: Caravaggio and the Baroque (tenebrism)
topics.scope: dramatic light-dark; violent realism; the brawling painter
topics.framing_note: Pillar-1 Baroque + drama-of-the-mind (the brawling painter who killed a man and fled with a death sentence, painting his own guilt into a severed head). Cool-fact answer: tenebrism = the single shaft of light out of black that he invented and that defined Baroque drama. The violent biography is a real-fact hook, not a 'secretly bad' reveal (anti-pattern guard).

topics.name: Bernini — Baroque sculpture
topics.scope: Ecstasy of St. Teresa; Apollo and Daphne; marble made flesh
topics.framing_note: Framework names 'Bernini's Ecstasy of St. Teresa + Apollo and Daphne marble miracle.' The beauty-of-mechanism lead (§2): HOW marble was carved to look like fingers pressing into soft flesh, or Daphne's fingertips turning to laurel leaves mid-run. Treat the religious subject (St. Teresa's vision) on its own terms, no smug voice.

topics.name: Rembrandt — Dutch Golden Age
topics.scope: Night Watch; Anatomy Lesson; self-portraits; light
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Art History; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Framework names 'Rembrandt's Night Watch + Anatomy Lesson.' Pillar-1 Dutch keystone. Cool-fact answers: The Night Watch isn't a night scene — centuries of darkened varnish fooled everyone; it was trimmed on all sides to fit a wall, cropping figures out. The self-portrait series tracking one face from cocky youth to bankrupt old age = the human-at-the-breaking-point wonder.

topics.name: Vermeer — Girl with a Pearl Earring
topics.scope: Dutch domestic light; tiny output; camera obscura
topics.source: Core Knowledge; AP Art History; cultural literacy
topics.framing_note: Framework names Vermeer explicitly. Ordinary-ingenuity + beauty-of-mechanism: the possible camera-obscura use; barely ~34 surviving paintings from a whole career; the 'Dutch Mona Lisa' that is a tronie (a type-study), not a portrait of a known person. Quiet luminous interiors as the hook — ask the specific, not attribution.

topics.name: Velazquez — Las Meninas
topics.scope: Spanish court; mirror; painter in the frame
topics.source: AP Art History anchor work; AP Euro
topics.framing_note: Pillar-1 Spanish-Golden-Age peak. Cool-fact answer: the painting-about-painting — Velazquez paints HIMSELF at his easel, and the king and queen appear only as a small reflection in the back mirror, putting the royal couple (and the viewer) in the same spot. The puzzle of who is looking at whom is the wonder. Present on its own terms.

topics.name: Jacques-Louis David and Neoclassicism
topics.scope: Oath of the Horatii; Death of Marat; Revolution's painter
topics.source: AP Art History anchor work; AP Euro
topics.framing_note: Art as revolutionary propaganda — the ideas-strand crossover into the French Revolution (Pillar 1 Enlightenment/Terror thread, where Lavoisier was guillotined). Honest, not preachy (§4): David was the Revolution's image-maker AND voted for the king's death AND later painted Napoleon's coronation — state plainly, no editorial. Cool-fact: Death of Marat as a deliberate secular pietà, idealizing a real political murder.

topics.name: Goya — The Third of May 1808
topics.scope: firing-squad painting; the dark late works
topics.framing_note: The first modern protest painting of war's horror — fits the bank's honest-about-violence stance (§4, state what happened, don't twist it). Cool-fact answer: the central victim's pose echoes the crucifixion, with a wound in the hand, turning a Napoleonic firing-squad atrocity into something timeless. The 'Black Paintings' Goya painted straight onto his own house walls in deaf isolation = drama-of-the-mind hook.

topics.name: Romanticism — Delacroix and Turner
topics.scope: Liberty Leading the People; Turner's storms of light
